nodes.title: Solutions of y_1 + ⋯ + y_n = 1 in a group of finite rank lie in few subspaces (Evertse–Schlickewei–Schmidt Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 2 and let Γ be a subgroup of (Q̄^*)^n of finite rank r. Then the set of y ∈ Q̄^n with y_1 + ⋯ + y_n = 1 (2.6) of the form y = x ∗ z with x ∈ Γ, z ∈ (Q̄^*)^n and h(z) ≤ n^{−1}exp(−(4n)^{3n})(1 + h(x)) (2.10) is contained in the union of at most B(n, r) = exp((5n)^{3n}(r + 1)) proper linear subspaces of Q̄^n. Here ∗ is coordinatewise multiplication and h(x) = log H(x) with H(x) = ∏_v max(1, ‖x_1‖_v, …, ‖x_n‖_v) the absolute multiplicative height.
hypotheses: Γ ⊆ (Q̄^*)^n of finite rank r (not necessarily finitely generated)
h is the absolute logarithmic Weil height (Mathlib: logHeight over a number field containing the coordinates, normalised by the degree)
proofSteps: Proved in ESS §§6–12: §6 reduces to Proposition 6.2; §7 heights in multiplicative groups; §8 special points; §9 properties of large special solutions; §10 large solutions via the quantitative Parametric Subspace Theorem for twisted heights with the special forms X_1, …, X_n, X_1 + ⋯ + X_n (Evertse–Schlickewei 2002, Theorem 2.1, improved by parametric-subspace-theorem, EF Theorem 1.1); §11 small solutions via a gap principle; §12 proof of Proposition 6.2.
These sections are not decomposed here (recorded as a gap); the node's only external input is parametric-subspace-theorem in the special case (1.5)–(1.6) of EF.
acceptance: With z = (1, …, 1) the theorem covers all solutions y ∈ Γ of y_1 + ⋯ + y_n = 1, which is how it enters uniform-bound-nondegenerate-solutions.
The bound depends only on n and r, not on Γ or the field.

nodes.title: Uniform bound for non-degenerate solutions in a group of finite rank (Evertse–Schlickewei–Schmidt Theorem 1.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, n ≥ 1, Γ a subgroup of (K^*)^n of finite rank r, and a = (a_1, …, a_n) ∈ (K^*)^n. Then a_1x_1 + ⋯ + a_nx_n = 1 (1.1) has at most A(n, r) = exp((6n)^{3n}(r + 1)) non-degenerate solutions x ∈ Γ.
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (the source takes K algebraically closed; any K embeds in its algebraic closure without changing the solution set)
Γ ⊆ (K^*)^n of finite rank r: some finitely generated Γ_0 ⊆ Γ of rank r has Γ/Γ_0 torsion
Non-degenerate: no non-empty subsum vanishes
proofSteps: Reduction to K = Q̄ (ESS Lemma 3.2): it suffices to bound any finite set M = {x_1, …, x_m} of non-degenerate solutions. Apply specialization-to-algebraic-numbers to the finite set U of the a_j, the coordinates x_{ij}, all subsums Σ_{j∈I}a_jx_{ij}, all differences x_{i_1,j} − x_{i_2,j}, and the inverses of the non-zero ones. The images x'_i are distinct non-degenerate solutions of Σ φ(a_j)y_j = 1 in the image of the group generated by M, which has rank ≤ r (nondegenerate-solution, map).

Case K = Q̄ (ESS §4), induction on n (n = 1 trivial): with Γ' generated by a and Γ (rank ≤ r + 1), unit-equation-subspace-bound-algebraic (z = 1) puts all solutions into B(n, r + 1) proper subspaces. On a subspace Σ_{i∈I} b_ix_i = 0 (#I ≥ 2), for each J ⊆ I with Σ_{i∈J} b_ix_i = 0 minimal, write w_i = x_i/x_1 (i ∈ J) and split Γ → Γ_1 (ratios) with kernel Γ_2, ranks r_1 + r_2 = r; induction bounds the (w_i) by A(#J − 1, r_1) and the remaining equation b'x' + Σ_{i∉J} a'_ix'_i = 1 in Γ_2-cosets by A(n − #J + 1, r_2).
Combine: at most 2^n A(n − 1, r) solutions per subspace, and 2^n A(n − 1, r) B(n, r + 1) < A(n, r).
acceptance: n = 1: at most one solution.
Non-degeneracy is necessary: x_1 − x_2 + x_3 = 1 has infinitely many degenerate solutions with x_1 = x_2 in any infinite Γ.

nodes.title: The S-unit equation theorem: finitely many non-degenerate solutions (Evertse Theorems 8.12 and 8.13; van der Poorten–Schlickewei, Evertse, Laurent)
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic 0, Γ a finitely generated subgroup of K^*, n ≥ 1 and α_1, …, α_n ∈ K^*. Then α_1x_1 + ⋯ + α_nx_n = 1 (8.14) has only finitely many non-degenerate solutions (x_1, …, x_n) ∈ Γ^n. For n = 2 every solution with x, y ∈ Γ is non-degenerate, so ax + by = 1 has finitely many solutions (Lang's theorem, Evertse 8.12). The known proofs for n ≥ 3 are ineffective; for n = 2 and K a number field an effective proof exists (DT.4).
hypotheses: K of characteristic 0 (any, not only number fields)
Γ ⊆ K^* finitely generated
α_i ∈ K^*
Non-degenerate in the sense of nondegenerate-solution
proofSteps: Γ^n ⊆ (K^*)^n is finitely generated, of finite rank r ≤ n·rank(Γ).
By uniform-bound-nondegenerate-solutions the equation has at most A(n, r) non-degenerate solutions in Γ^n; in particular finitely many.
For n = 2, a solution of ax + by = 1 with x, y ∈ Γ has ax ≠ 0 and by ≠ 0, so it is non-degenerate.
Over ℚ the source proves the case Γ ⊂ ℚ^* directly (s-unit-equation-over-rationals); it agrees with this node.
acceptance: K = ℚ: consistent with s-unit-equation-over-rationals.
DT.2 acceptance: finiteness is separate from effectivity; the bound A(n, r) counts solutions but does not locate them.
Application: skolem-mahler-lech-simple-roots uses this theorem with Γ generated by complex, possibly transcendental, ratios of roots.

nodes.title: Non-degenerate linear recurrences
nodes.statement: A linear recurrence E over ℂ (Mathlib's `LinearRecurrence ℂ`: an order k and coefficients (E.coeffs i)_{i<k}, with solutions u satisfying u(h + k) = Σ_{i<k} E.coeffs i · u(h + i)) is non-degenerate if its characteristic polynomial E.charPoly = X^k − Σ_{i<k} E.coeffs i X^i has non-zero constant term (so all its roots are non-zero; Evertse's c_k ≠ 0) and for any two distinct roots θ ≠ θ' of E.charPoly, the quotient θ/θ' is not a root of unity (¬ IsOfFinOrder (θ/θ')). A linear recurrence sequence is non-degenerate if its minimal recurrence is; a sequence satisfying some non-degenerate recurrence is non-degenerate, since the characteristic polynomial of the minimal recurrence divides that of any recurrence it satisfies.
hypotheses: E : LinearRecurrence ℂ
Evertse's u_h = c_1u_{h−1} + ⋯ + c_ku_{h−k} corresponds to E.coeffs i = c_{k−i}; his companion polynomial f_U is E.charPoly
proofSteps: IsNondegenerate E :⇔ E.charPoly.coeff 0 ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ θ ∈ E.charPoly.roots, ∀ θ' ∈ E.charPoly.roots, θ ≠ θ' → ¬ IsOfFinOrder (θ / θ').
acceptance: Fibonacci u_{h+2} = u_{h+1} + u_h: roots (1 ± √5)/2 with ratio −(3 + √5)/2, of absolute value ≠ 1, hence not a root of unity: non-degenerate.
u_{h+2} = −u_h: roots ±i with ratio −1, a root of unity: degenerate (and u = (0, 1, 0, −1, …) has infinitely many zeros).

nodes.title: Skolem–Mahler–Lech for simple roots via the S-unit equation (Evertse Theorem 8.18, case e_i = 1)
nodes.statement: Let m ≥ 1, θ_1, …, θ_m non-zero complex numbers such that no quotient θ_i/θ_j (i ≠ j) is a root of unity, and g_1, …, g_m ∈ ℂ not all 0. Then g_1θ_1^h + ⋯ + g_mθ_m^h = 0 has only finitely many solutions h ∈ ℤ_{≥0}. Equivalently: a non-zero linear recurrence sequence U over ℂ satisfying a non-degenerate recurrence whose characteristic polynomial has no multiple roots has a finite zero set Z_U = {h ≥ 0 : u_h = 0}.
hypotheses: θ_i ∈ ℂ^*, θ_i/θ_j not a root of unity for i ≠ j (in particular the θ_i are distinct)
g_i ∈ ℂ constants, not all zero (U ≠ 0; the source's first formulation omits this, see sourceIssues)
Simple roots only: the general case with polynomial coefficients g_i(h) is proved by p-adic analysis and is not an S-unit application
proofSteps: Discard the indices with g_i = 0 (the hypothesis persists); induction on the number m of remaining terms. m = 1: g_1θ_1^h ≠ 0.
m ≥ 2: put a_i := −g_i/g_m ∈ ℂ^* and β_i := θ_i/θ_m (i < m); the equation becomes a_1β_1^h + ⋯ + a_{m−1}β_{m−1}^h = 1 (8.21), and no β_i and no β_i/β_j (i ≠ j) is a root of unity.

Apply s-unit-equation-finiteness with K = ℂ, Γ generated by β_1, …, β_{m−1}: finitely many non-degenerate solutions (β_1^h, …, β_{m−1}^h); since β_1 is not a root of unity, h ↦ β_1^h is injective, so finitely many h give non-degenerate solutions.

For the other h some subsum Σ_{i∈I} a_iβ_i^h vanishes with ∅ ≠ I ⊆ {1, …, m − 1} (the source writes {1, …, m}); multiplying by θ_m^h, Σ_{i∈I} g_iθ_i^h = 0, an equation with fewer terms satisfying the hypotheses, so the induction hypothesis leaves finitely many h for each of the finitely many I.
Recurrence form: if E has simple roots θ_1, …, θ_k, every solution is u_h = Σ g_iθ_i^h (the closed form requested from ClassicalArithmeticCompletion:CA.2), and u ≠ 0 means some g_i ≠ 0.
acceptance: u_h = 2^h + 3^h − 5^h (Evertse’s example, roots 2, 3, 5, non-degenerate): u_0 = 1, u_1 = 0 and u_h < 0 for h ≥ 2, so the zero set is {1}.
Degenerate counterexample: u_h = i^h + (−i)^h vanishes for all odd h (roots with ratio −1).
Zero sequence: excluded by 'not all g_i zero'.

nodes.title: Uniform bound for the zeros of simple linear recurrences (Evertse–Schlickewei–Schmidt Theorem 1.2)
nodes.statement: Let K be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, n ≥ 3, and let u_m = a_1α_1^m + ⋯ + a_nα_n^m (m ∈ ℤ) with a_i ∈ K^* and pairwise distinct α_i ∈ K^* (a simple linear recurrence sequence of order n, indexed by ℤ). Then there are integers k_1, …, k_{q_1} and arithmetic progressions T_i = {a'_i + tv_i : t ∈ ℤ} (v_i ≠ 0, i = 1, …, q_2) with q_1 + q_2 ≤ exp((6n)^{3n}) such that S(u) := {k ∈ ℤ : u_k = 0} = {k_1, …, k_{q_1}} ∪ T_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ T_{q_2}. If moreover no α_i/α_j (i ≠ j) is a root of unity, then #S(u) ≤ exp((6n)^{3n}).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic 0 (any field of characteristic 0 embeds in one)
n ≥ 3 (for n = 2 the zero set is empty or one point, or, in the degenerate case, a union of progressions)
Simple: distinct roots, constant coefficients a_i ≠ 0
proofSteps: Induction on n, with W(n) := exp((6n)^{3n}) and single integers counted as progressions of difference 0 (ESS §5).

Zeros k for which no proper subsum of Σ a_iα_i^k vanishes give non-degenerate solutions ((α_1/α_n)^k, …, (α_{n−1}/α_n)^k) of Σ_{i<n}(−a_i/a_n)x_i = 1 in the rank-≤1 group generated by (α_1/α_n, …, α_{n−1}/α_n); by uniform-bound-nondegenerate-solutions there are at most A(n − 1, 1) such solutions, and each determines an arithmetic progression of k.

Zeros with a vanishing proper subsum Σ_{i∈I} a_iα_i^k = 0 (2 ≤ #I ≤ n − 2) also satisfy Σ_{i∉I} a_iα_i^k = 0; by induction each set is a union of at most W(#I), resp. W(n − #I), progressions, and intersections of progressions are progressions: at most 2^n W(n − 1) progressions in total.

Non-degenerate case: if S(u) contained {a + vt} with v ≠ 0, the Vandermonde determinant det(α_i^{vt})_{i, t<n} would vanish, forcing α_i^v = α_j^v for some i ≠ j, contradicting non-degeneracy; so S(u) is a finite union of at most W(n) points.
acceptance: Quantitative form of skolem-mahler-lech-simple-roots: the bound depends only on the order n.

Degenerate example: u_m = 1 + (−1)^m (roots 1, −1, ratio −1) vanishes exactly on the odd integers, one arithmetic progression; the theorem bounds the number of progressions (here n = 2, below the theorem's range, where the bound is immediate).
Theorem 8.19 of Evertse (Schmidt 2000) extends the non-degenerate bound to non-simple recurrences with a triply exponential bound; not proved in the sources read.

nodes.title: Twisted height H_{L,c,Q} (Evertse–Ferretti (2.13)–(2.15))
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with normalised absolute values ‖·‖_v (v ∈ M_K), n ≥ 1, L = (L_i^{(v)}) a tuple of linear forms in K[X_1, …, X_n] satisfying (2.5)–(2.6) and c = (c_{iv}) a tuple of reals satisfying (2.7) (for the theorems also (2.8)–(2.9)). For a real Q ≥ 1 the twisted height is H_{L,c,Q}(x) := ∏_{v ∈ M_K} max_{1≤i≤n} (‖L_i^{(v)}(x)‖_v · Q^{−c_{iv}}) for x ∈ K^n. For x ∈ Q̄^n choose a finite extension E ⊇ K with x ∈ E^n and put L_i^{(w)} := L_i^{(v)}, c_{iw} := d(w|v)c_{iv} for w | v, d(w|v) := [E_w : K_v]/[E : K], and H_{L,c,Q}(x) := ∏_{w ∈ M_E} max_i ‖L_i^{(w)}(x)‖_w Q^{−c_{iw}}; this does not depend on E. H_{L,c,Q}(0) = 0; for x ≠ 0 all factors are non-zero and almost all equal 1. With L_i^{(v)} = X_i and c = 0 it is the absolute multiplicative height H(x) = ∏_v max_i ‖x_i‖_v.
hypotheses: K a number field; normalised absolute values with the product formula
(2.5)–(2.7) (and (2.8)–(2.9) as normalisations used by the theorems)
Q ≥ 1 real
proofSteps: Define the local factor at v as max_i ‖L_i^{(v)}(x)‖_v Q^{−c_{iv}} and take the product over v; by (2.5)–(2.7) and x ≠ 0 only finitely many factors differ from 1 (for almost all v the forms are v-integral with unit determinant and c_{iv} = 0, so the factor is ‖x‖_v, which is 1 for almost all v), so the product is a finite product (a finprod over the places).
Independence of E: by d(w|v) summing to 1 over w | v (EF (2.3)) and ‖x‖_w = ‖x‖_v^{d(w|v)} for x ∈ K (EF (2.2)).

Projective invariance H(αx) = H(x) (α ≠ 0) follows from the product formula; Galois invariance H(σx) = H(x) for σ ∈ Gal(Q̄/K) (EF Lemma 4.1) from the fact that σ permutes the places above each v preserving local degrees.
acceptance: c = 0, L = coordinates: H_{L,0,Q}(x) = H(x), the absolute height (for K = ℚ and primitive x ∈ ℤ^n, max_i |x_i|).

nodes.title: Successive infima λ_i(Q) of a twisted height and their subspaces (Evertse–Ferretti §9)
nodes.statement: In the setting of twisted-height, for Q ≥ 1 and λ ≥ 0 let T(Q, λ) be the Q̄-vector space spanned by {x ∈ Q̄^n : H_{L,c,Q}(x) ≤ λ}. The successive infima are λ_i(Q) := inf{λ ≥ 0 : dim T(Q, λ) ≥ i} (i = 1, …, n), and T_i(Q) := ∩_{λ > λ_i(Q)} T(Q, λ). Over Q̄ the infima need not be attained. The spaces T_i(Q) are defined over K (Galois invariance of the twisted height), and if λ_k(Q) < λ_{k+1}(Q) then dim T_k(Q) = k and T(Q, λ) = T_k(Q) for λ_k(Q) < λ < λ_{k+1}(Q) (EF Lemma 9.1).
hypotheses: Setting of twisted-height with (2.4)–(2.7)

Points range over Q̄^n (all finite extensions of K); the Lean prototype uses K-rational points, and the absolute version is the infimum over finite extensions E ⊇ K of the E-rational versions with the lifted data (2.14)
proofSteps: λ_i(Q) is an infimum of a non-empty set of reals bounded below by 0 (T(Q, λ) = Q̄^n for large λ, since H_{L,c,Q}(e_j) < ∞).
EF Lemma 9.1: (i) T(Q, λ) is Gal(Q̄/K)-stable by EF Lemma 4.1, hence defined over K; (ii) dim T(Q, λ) = k for λ_k < λ < λ_{k+1} since dimension jumps exactly at the infima and T(Q, λ) grows with λ.
acceptance: For c = 0 and L = coordinates, λ_i(Q) are the successive minima of the absolute height, λ_1 = ⋯ = λ_n = 1.

uses.how: Minkowski-type bounds for λ_1(Q) ⋯ λ_n(Q)
a gap λ_k(Q) ≤ Q^{−δ/(n−1)}λ_{k+1}(Q) whenever λ_1(Q) ≤ Q^{−δ}
limit behaviour of λ_i(Q) as Q → ∞
Davenport's lemma produces vectors adapted to λ_1(Q), …, λ_n(Q)

nodes.title: Height H_2(T) of a linear subspace (Evertse–Ferretti §6.3; Schmidt)
nodes.statement: For y ∈ Q̄^N with y ∈ E^N (E a number field) put H_2(y) := ∏_{w ∈ M_E} ‖y‖_{w,2}, where ‖y‖_{w,2} := (Σ_i |σ_w(y_i)|²)^{s(w)/2} with s(w) := [E_w : ℝ]/[E : ℚ] at infinite w and ‖y‖_{w,2} := max_i ‖y_i‖_w at finite w; it is independent of E, and n^{−1/2}H_2(y) ≤ H(y) ≤ H_2(y). For p vectors x_1, …, x_p ∈ Q̄^n the exterior product x_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ x_p ∈ Q̄^N (N = C(n, p)) is the vector of p × p minors of the matrix with rows x_i, indexed by the p-subsets of {1, …, n} in lexicographic order. For a linear subspace T ⊆ Q̄^n: H_2(T) := 1 if T = {0} or T = Q̄^n, and H_2(T) := H_2(x_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ x_p) if dim T = p ∈ (0, n) and {x_1, …, x_p} is any basis of T (independent of the basis by the product formula). Linear forms are identified with their coefficient vectors, which defines H_2(L) and H_2(V) for spaces V of linear forms.
hypotheses: Absolute values normalised as in twisted-height; s(w) = 0 at finite places
Plücker coordinates in lexicographic order
proofSteps: A change of basis multiplies x_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ x_p by the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix, a non-zero scalar, and H_2 is invariant under non-zero scalars by the product formula.
Independence of the field E as for the absolute height.
acceptance: For a rational subspace T ⊆ ℚ^n, H_2(T) is the covolume of the lattice T ∩ ℤ^n in T ⊗ ℝ (the Euclidean norm of the wedge of a ℤ-basis): the notion of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.0 for non-full-rank lattices.

uses.how: the non-vanishing result needs H_2(T_h)^{r_h} large for (N − 1)-dimensional subspaces T_h
lower bound H_2(T_k(Q)) ≥ Q^{δ/3Rn} in the semistable case
upper bound H_2(T_i) ≤ H_2^{4n} for the filtration subspaces, giving effectivity of the exceptional subspace
H_2(T^⊥) = H_2(T) and the compatibility with exterior powers

nodes.title: Weights of subspaces and the exceptional subspace T(L, c) (Evertse–Ferretti (2.19)–(2.21), Lemmas 15.1–15.2)
nodes.statement: In the setting of twisted-height, for a linear subspace U ⊆ Q̄^n of dimension k and v ∈ M_K put w_v(U) := 0 if k = 0 and otherwise w_v(U) := min{c_{i_1v} + ⋯ + c_{i_kv} : L^{(v)}_{i_1}|_U, …, L^{(v)}_{i_k}|_U linearly independent}; the weight is w(U) := Σ_v w_v(U) (a finite sum by (2.7)). The weight is supermodular: w(U_1 ∩ U_2) + w(U_1 + U_2) ≥ w(U_1) + w(U_2) (EF Lemma 15.1). There is a unique proper subspace T = T(L, c) of Q̄^n such that w(T)/(n − dim T) ≥ w(U)/(n − dim U) for every proper subspace U, and dim T is minimal subject to this; T is defined over K (EF Lemma 15.2 with V = Q̄^n, where w(Q̄^n) = 0 by (2.8)). (L, c) is semistable if T(L, c) = {0}, equivalently w(U) ≤ 0 for every proper U.
hypotheses: Setting of twisted-height with (2.4)–(2.8)
Weights use the restrictions of the forms to U; for U ⊆ Q̄^n and forms over K
proofSteps: Local weights (15.3)–(15.4): ordering c_{1v} ≤ ⋯ ≤ c_{nv}, w_v(U) = Σ_{i ∈ I_v(U)} c_{iv} with I_v(U) the greedy set of indices, and w_v(U) = c_{1v} dim U + Σ_i (c_{i+1,v} − c_{iv}) dim(U ∩ U_{iv}), U_{iv} := {L_1^{(v)} = ⋯ = L_i^{(v)} = 0}.
Lemma 15.1: supermodularity follows from the last formula, c_{i+1,v} − c_{iv} ≥ 0, dim(U_1 ∩ U_2) + dim(U_1 + U_2) = dim U_1 + dim U_2 and U ∩ (U_1 + U_2) ⊇ (U ∩ U_1) + (U ∩ U_2).

Lemma 15.2(i): µ(V, U) := (w(V) − w(U))/(dim V − dim U) takes finitely many values, so a minimiser exists; take one of minimal dimension. (ii): by supermodularity µ(V, U ∩ T) ≤ µ(V, U) for any proper U; this forces uniqueness (two minimisers of minimal dimension would give a smaller one, their intersection) and Galois stability (σ(T) is again such a subspace), hence T is defined over K.
acceptance: c = 0: all weights vanish and T = {0} (semistable).
K = ℚ, n = 2, L^{(v)} = coordinates, c_∞ = (−1, 1), other c = 0: w(ℚ̄e_2) = 1, w(ℚ̄e_1) = −1, w(other lines) = −1, so T = Q̄e_2.
EF Lemma 15.3: for L^{(v)} ⊂ {X_1, …, X_n, X_1 + ⋯ + X_n}, T = {x : Σ_{j ∈ I_i} x_j = 0, i = 1, …, p} for pairwise disjoint I_1, …, I_p.

uses.how: the interval result holds outside the exceptional subspace T(L, c)
semistability T = {0} (condition (8.9)) is the hypothesis of the semistable interval result
w(T) ≤ 0 gives the lower bound for H_2(T_k(Q))
the effectively computable exceptional subspaces of Vojta's refinement

nodes.title: The filtration of Q̄^n attached to (L, c) (Evertse–Ferretti Lemma 15.4)
nodes.statement: In the setting of weight-and-exceptional-subspace, for a subspace V ⊆ Q̄^n defined over K let B(V, L, c) be the upper convex hull of the points P(U) := (dim U, w(U)) for subspaces U ⊆ V. There is a unique filtration {0} = T_0 ⊊ T_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ T_{r−1} ⊊ T_r = V such that P(T_0), …, P(T_r) are precisely the vertices of B(V, L, c); the T_i are defined over K, and T_{r−1} is the subspace T of EF Lemma 15.2(i) for V (for V = Q̄^n, T_{r−1} = T(L, c)). The slopes µ(T_l, T_{l−1}) := (w(T_l) − w(T_{l−1}))/(dim T_l − dim T_{l−1}) are strictly decreasing in l. It is the analogue of the Harder–Narasimhan filtration of Faltings–Wüstholz.
hypotheses: Setting of weight-and-exceptional-subspace; V defined over K
proofSteps: Induction on dim V: the only candidate for T_{r−1} is the subspace T of Lemma 15.2(i) (defined over K); apply the induction hypothesis to T.

The points P(T_0), …, P(T_{r−1}), P(V) are vertices of a concave piecewise-linear graph (since µ(T_{r−1}, T_{r−2}) > µ(V, T_{r−1})); every P(U) lies on or below it: for U ⊆ T_{r−1} by induction, otherwise by Lemma 15.2(ii) µ(V, U ∩ T_{r−1}) ≤ µ(V, U) and concavity.
acceptance: c = 0: the filtration is {0} ⊊ Q̄^n (r = 1).
Example of weight-and-exceptional-subspace: {0} ⊊ Q̄e_2 ⊊ Q̄².

uses.how: the successive infima λ_i(Q) behave like Q^{−µ(T_l, T_{l−1})} on the l-th block of the filtration, and T_{d_l}(Q) = T_l for large Q

nodes.title: Minkowski's second theorem for twisted heights over Q̄ (Evertse–Ferretti Proposition 9.2; Roy–Thunder)
nodes.statement: Let (L, c) satisfy (2.4)–(2.7) and put α := Σ_{v ∈ M_K} Σ_{i=1}^n c_{iv}. Then for every Q ≥ 1, n^{−n/2} Δ_L Q^{−α} ≤ λ_1(Q) ⋯ λ_n(Q) ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/2} Δ_L Q^{−α}, where λ_i(Q) are the successive infima of H_{L,c,Q} over Q̄^n and Δ_L = ∏_v ‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v. In particular, under (2.8) (α = 0), n^{−n/2}Δ_L ≤ λ_1(Q) ⋯ λ_n(Q) ≤ 2^{n(n−1)/2}Δ_L.
hypotheses: Standing notation (EF §§1–2): K ⊂ Q̄ a number field with places M_K and normalised absolute values ‖·‖_v (‖x‖_v = |σ_v(x)|^{[K_v:ℝ]/[K:ℚ]} at infinite v; the extension of |·|_p^{[K_v:ℚ_p]/[K:ℚ]} at v | p), which satisfy the product formula ∏_v ‖x‖_v = 1 on K^*; n ≥ 2; L = (L_i^{(v)} : v ∈ M_K, 1 ≤ i ≤ n) linear forms in K[X_1, …, X_n] with {L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)}} linearly independent for each v (2.5) and {L_1, …, L_r} := ∪_v {L_i^{(v)}} finite (2.6); c = (c_{iv}) reals with c_{iv} = 0 for all but finitely many v (2.7), Σ_i c_{iv} = 0 (2.8), Σ_v max_i c_{iv} ≤ 1 (2.9); 0 < δ ≤ 1, R ≥ r (2.10); Δ_L := ∏_v ‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v (2.11) and H_L := ∏_v max_{i_1<⋯<i_n} ‖det(L_{i_1}, …, L_{i_n})‖_v (2.12).
Successive infima over Q̄^n (absolute), not over K^n
proofSteps: EF: 'This is a reformulation of [11, Corollary 7.2]' (Evertse–Schlickewei 2002, §7), which is an easy consequence of the absolute analogue of Minkowski's second theorem due to Roy and Thunder (J. reine angew. Math. 476 (1996)).

The Roy–Thunder theorem generalises the adelic Minkowski second theorem of Bombieri–Vaaler (Invent. Math. 73 (1983)) over a number field, which in turn rests on the classical Minkowski second theorem for a convex symmetric body and a lattice in ℝ^N (requested from GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic:GN.1).
Neither the reformulation in Evertse–Schlickewei §7 nor the Roy–Thunder theorem is decomposed here (gap); Roy–Thunder's paper is not publicly available.
acceptance: n = 1 (formally): λ_1(Q) = H_{L,c,Q}(1) = Δ_L Q^{−α}.
L = coordinates, c = 0: Δ_L = 1 and all λ_i = 1, consistent with the bounds.

nodes.title: Gap principle: one subspace for a short range of Q (Evertse–Ferretti Proposition 4.2)
nodes.statement: Assume (2.4)–(2.10) and let A ≥ n^{1/δ}. Then there is a single proper linear subspace T_0 of Q̄^n, defined over K, such that for every Q with A ≤ Q < A^{1+δ/2}, {x ∈ Q̄^n : H_{L,c,Q}(x) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}} ⊂ T_0.
hypotheses: Standing notation (EF §§1–2): K ⊂ Q̄ a number field with places M_K and normalised absolute values ‖·‖_v (‖x‖_v = |σ_v(x)|^{[K_v:ℝ]/[K:ℚ]} at infinite v; the extension of |·|_p^{[K_v:ℚ_p]/[K:ℚ]} at v | p), which satisfy the product formula ∏_v ‖x‖_v = 1 on K^*; n ≥ 2; L = (L_i^{(v)} : v ∈ M_K, 1 ≤ i ≤ n) linear forms in K[X_1, …, X_n] with {L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)}} linearly independent for each v (2.5) and {L_1, …, L_r} := ∪_v {L_i^{(v)}} finite (2.6); c = (c_{iv}) reals with c_{iv} = 0 for all but finitely many v (2.7), Σ_i c_{iv} = 0 (2.8), Σ_v max_i c_{iv} ≤ 1 (2.9); 0 < δ ≤ 1, R ≥ r (2.10); Δ_L := ∏_v ‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v (2.11) and H_L := ∏_v max_{i_1<⋯<i_n} ‖det(L_{i_1}, …, L_{i_n})‖_v (2.12).
proofSteps: Let Q ∈ [A, A^{1+δ/2}) and x ≠ 0 with H_{L,c,Q}(x) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}. With θ_w := max_i c_{iw} (Σ_i c_{iw} = 0, Σ_w θ_w ≤ 1): at places with θ_w > 0 the local factor at Q exceeds that at A times A^{−θ_wδ/2}; taking products, H_{L,c,A}(x) < Δ_L^{1/n}A^{−δ/2} (4.3).

Let T_0 be the span of all x with (4.3); it is Gal(Q̄/K)-stable (EF Lemma 4.1, an API item of twisted-height), hence defined over K. It suffices to show det(x_1, …, x_n) = 0 for x_1, …, x_n with (4.3).

At infinite places write the forms through an embedding and bound ‖det(x_1, …, x_n)‖_w ≤ Δ_w^{−1} n^{ns(w)/2} H_{1w} ⋯ H_{nw} by Hadamard's inequality (hadamard-inequality) (4.5); at finite places the ultrametric inequality gives the same without n^{ns(w)/2} (4.6), using Σ_i c_{iw} = 0.
Taking the product over w ∈ M_E: ∏_w ‖det(x_1, …, x_n)‖_w ≤ Δ_L^{−1}n^{n/2}∏_j H_{L,c,A}(x_j) < n^{n/2}A^{−nδ/2} ≤ 1, so det(x_1, …, x_n) = 0 by the product formula (NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one).
acceptance: The gap principle is effective: T_0 is spanned by points of explicitly bounded twisted height.
Case n = 2 is the classical gap principle for Roth's theorem (Evertse survey, Proposition 1.3): two good approximations of comparable height lie on the same line.

nodes.title: Davenport's lemma for twisted heights (Evertse–Ferretti Lemma 11.3)
nodes.statement: Assume (8.1)–(8.9) (the semistable setting of interval-result-semistable-case, with the non-archimedean place v_0 of (8.8)), fix Q ≥ 1, let λ_i = λ_i(Q) be the successive infima of H_{L,c,Q}, choose ε > 0 with (1 + ε)²λ_i < λ_{i+1} whenever λ_i < λ_{i+1} and (1 + ε)^{n+1}·n·2^{n²} < 3^{n²} (11.1), and linearly independent g_1, …, g_n ∈ Q̄^n with H_{L,c,Q}(g_i) ≤ (1 + ε/2)λ_i (11.2). Then there exist a finite extension E of K, a permutation π of {1, …, n} and vectors h_j = h_j(Q) ∈ E^n (j = 1, …, n) with span{h_1, …, h_j} = span{g_1, …, g_j} for all j (11.5), ‖L_i^{(w)}(h_j)‖_w ≤ n^{−s(w)}Q^{c_{iw}} for all i, j and all w ∈ M_E not above v_0 (11.6), and ‖L_{π(i)}^{(w)}(h_j)‖_w ≤ (3^{n²} min(λ_i, λ_j))^{d(w|v_0)} for all i, j and w | v_0 (11.7).
hypotheses: s(w) = [E_w : ℝ]/[E : ℚ] at infinite w, 0 at finite w
proofSteps: EF Lemma 11.1 (= Evertse–Schlickewei Lemma 6.3): for positive reals A_u (u ∈ M_F), almost all 1, with ∏A_u > 1, there are a finite extension E and α ∈ E^* with ‖α‖_w ≤ A_u^{d(w|u)}.
EF Lemma 11.2: rescaling g_j by such scalars α_j gives g'_j with the local bounds (11.3)–(11.4).

EF: 'The proof is the same as that of [11, Lemma 9.2], except for some small modifications': Davenport's triangular change of basis applied to g'_1, …, g'_n at the place v_0 (Evertse–Schlickewei 2002, §9), with (11.1) in place of their (9.15); it yields (11.5)–(11.7) with 2n^{2n}(1 + ε)^{n+1} in place of 3^{n²}.
The proof of Evertse–Schlickewei Lemma 9.2 is not decomposed here (gap).
acceptance: n = 2: the lemma reduces to the classical Davenport lemma for a reduced basis of a two-dimensional lattice.
(11.5) says the flags generated by the g_j and the h_j coincide.

nodes.title: Roth's lemma in Evertse's sharp form (Evertse 1995 Theorem 3; Evertse 1996 Lemma 23)
nodes.statement: Let m ≥ 2, d = (d_1, …, d_m) positive integers and 0 < Θ ≤ 1 with d_h/d_{h+1} ≥ 2m²/Θ for h = 1, …, m − 1. Let F ∈ Q̄[X_{11}, X_{12}, …, X_{m1}, X_{m2}] be non-zero and homogeneous of degree d_h in (X_{h1}, X_{h2}) for each h, and let x_h ∈ Q̄² ∖ {0} (h = 1, …, m) with H(x_h)^{d_h} ≥ (e^{d_1+⋯+d_m}H(F))^{(3m²/Θ)^m}. Then F has index < mΘ at x = (x_1, …, x_m) with respect to d: there is a multi-index i = (i_{hl}) with Σ_h (i_{h1} + i_{h2})/d_h < mΘ such that the divided derivative F_i = (∏_{h,l} (1/i_{hl}!) ∂^{i_{hl}}/∂X_{hl}^{i_{hl}}) F does not vanish at x.
hypotheses: m ≥ 2; degrees decreasing fast: d_h/d_{h+1} ≥ 2m²/Θ
H is the absolute height of a point / of the coefficient vector of F
Index formulated through divided derivatives in all block variables
proofSteps: Evertse 1996 recalls it as 'Theorem 3 of [6]', where [6] is Evertse, 'An explicit version of Faltings' Product Theorem and an improvement of Roth's lemma', Acta Arith. 73 (1995); its proof makes Faltings' Product Theorem explicit.

Not decomposed here (gap). It is the only 'Roth machinery' input of the Subspace Theorem proof followed here; Roth's original lemma (1955), with worse constants, would serve the qualitative theorem but belongs with Roth's proof (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.1).
acceptance: m = 1 is excluded (Liouville-type statements suffice there).
The height condition is what forces non-vanishing: for x_h of small height F may vanish to high order at x.

nodes.title: Non-vanishing of an auxiliary polynomial at grid points (Evertse–Ferretti Proposition 12.1; Evertse 1996 Lemma 26)
nodes.statement: Let m, N ≥ 2, 0 < ε ≤ 1 and r_1, …, r_m positive integers with r_h/r_{h+1} ≥ 2m²/ε (h = 1, …, m − 1) (12.3). Let P ∈ Q̄[X_1, …, X_m] (blocks X_h = (X_{h1}, …, X_{hN})) be non-zero and homogeneous of degree r_h in X_h for each h, and let T_1, …, T_m be (N − 1)-dimensional linear subspaces of Q̄^N with H_2(T_h)^{r_h} ≥ (e^{r_1+⋯+r_m}H_2(P))^{(N−1)(3m²/ε)^m} (12.4). For each h let Γ_h be a grid of size N/ε in T_h (the set {Σ_i x_ia_i : x_i ∈ ℤ, |x_i| ≤ N/ε} for a basis a_1, …, a_{N−1} of T_h). Then there are x_h ∈ Γ_h ∖ {0} (h = 1, …, m) and i ∈ ℤ_{≥0}^{mN} with Σ_h (1/r_h)Σ_l i_{hl} ≤ 2mε (12.5) and P_i(x_1, …, x_m) ≠ 0 (12.6), where P_i = ∏_{h,l}(1/i_{hl}!)∂^{i_{hl}}/∂X_{hl}^{i_{hl}} P.
hypotheses: P multihomogeneous of degree (r_1, …, r_m); H_2(P) is H_2 of its coefficient vector
T_h hyperplanes of Q̄^N with (12.4); grids of size N/ε
proofSteps: EF recall this as Evertse 1996, Lemma 26, 'deduced from a sharp version of Roth's Lemma, and ultimately goes back to Faltings' Product Theorem'.

Evertse 1996 §7: Lemma 24 reduces the (N − 1)-dimensional subspace case to N = 2 by Schmidt's argument (LNM 785, pp. 192–194) and applies sharp-roths-lemma; Lemma 25 bounds the index of a non-zero polynomial at grid points; Lemma 26 combines them to get grid points with small index. These three lemmas (about five pages) are not decomposed here (gap).

The exponent (3m²/ε)^m in (12.4) is what makes the resulting interval result ineffective: it needs m approximations of rapidly increasing height.

nodes.title: Siegel's lemma with heights over a number field (Bombieri–Vaaler; Evertse–Ferretti Lemma 13.1)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with discriminant D_K and C_K := |D_K|^{1/(2[K:ℚ])}, let U, V be integers with V > U > 0, and L_1, …, L_U non-zero linear forms in K[X_1, …, X_V]. Then there is x ∈ K^V ∖ {0} with L_1(x) = ⋯ = L_U(x) = 0 and H_2(x) ≤ V^{1/2}C_K(H_2(L_1) ⋯ H_2(L_U))^{1/(V−U)}.

nodes.title: Construction of the auxiliary polynomial (Evertse–Ferretti Proposition 13.6)
nodes.statement: Assume (8.1)–(8.9), let k and N = C(n, k) be as in EF §11, and let the exterior-power forms L̂_l^{(v)} and exponents ĉ_{lv}, ĉ_{l,v_0}(Q) be as in (11.10)–(11.16). Let 0 < ε ≤ 1, m an integer with m ≥ 2nε^{−2}log(4R/ε) (13.22), r_1, …, r_m positive integers, and Q_1, …, Q_m reals each satisfying (11.8)–(11.9). Then there is a non-zero polynomial P ∈ K[X_1, …, X_m], homogeneous of degree r_h in the block X_h of N variables (type (13.9)), such that: (i) for every v ≠ v_0, every i with Σ_h (1/r_h)Σ_l i_{hl} ≤ 2mε (13.23) and every j ∈ U(r, i) with Σ_h (1/r_h)Σ_l ĉ_{lv}j_{hl} > 4mnε max_i c_{iv} (13.24), the coefficient d^{(v)}_{i,j}(a_P) of P_i in the coordinates L̂^{(v)} vanishes; (ii) for every i with (13.23) and j ∈ U(r, i) with Σ_h (1/r_h)Σ_l ĉ_{l,v_0}(Q_h)j_{hl} > −mδ/(nN) + 4mnε (13.26), d^{(v_0)}_{i,j}(a_P) = 0; (iii) H_2(P) ≤ (C_K(2^{3n}H_L^{R^n}))^{r_1+⋯+r_m}; (iv) the product over v of max_j ‖d^{(v)}_{i,j}(a_P)‖_v is bounded by (C_K 2^{6n}H_L^{2R^n})^{r_1+⋯+r_m} (13.29).
hypotheses: m as in (13.22)
proofSteps: EF Lemma 13.2 is Hoeffding's inequality (Mathlib: ProbabilityTheory.hasSubgaussianMGF_of_mem_Icc and ProbabilityTheory.HasSubgaussianMGF.measure_sum_ge_le_of_iIndepFun).

EF Lemma 13.3 (counting): for |ĉ_{hl}| ≤ γ, the number of j ∈ U(r) with Σ_h (1/r_h)Σ_l j_{hl}ĉ_{hl} ≥ (1/N)Σ_{h,l} ĉ_{hl} + mγε is at most e^{−mε²/2}V (V = #U(r)), by viewing j as uniformly random and applying Hoeffding to the independent block averages.

EF Lemma 13.4: the coefficients of P_i with respect to the coordinates L̂^{(v)} are linear forms d^{(v)}_{i,j} in the coefficient vector a_P with explicit bounds (change of coordinates by the inverse matrix).

EF Lemma 13.5 and the proof of Proposition 13.6: group the places v with c_v ≠ 0 into boundedly many classes (at most R^n choices of forms times ([2/ε] + 1)^n subcubes for the exponents), impose the vanishing conditions (i)–(ii) for one representative per class, count them by Lemma 13.3 (fewer than V/2 conditions), and solve with bombieri-vaaler-siegel-lemma to get the height bounds (iii)–(iv).
The individual lemmas 13.3–13.5 (about seven pages in total) are not split into separate nodes here.
acceptance: The construction replaces Schmidt's auxiliary polynomial by the Faltings–Wüstholz one: the vanishing conditions are imposed only in the directions of large weight, counted probabilistically.
m grows like ε^{−2}log R, which is where the quantitative bounds of EF come from.

nodes.title: Limit behaviour of the successive infima (Evertse–Ferretti Theorem 16.1)
nodes.statement: Let (L, c) satisfy (2.4)–(2.7) with n ≥ 1, let {0} = T_0 ⊊ T_1 ⊊ ⋯ ⊊ T_r = Q̄^n be the filtration of Q̄^n with respect to (L, c) (twisted-height-filtration), d_l := dim T_l, and µ(T_l, T_{l−1}) := (w(T_l) − w(T_{l−1}))/(d_l − d_{l−1}). For every δ > 0 there is Q_0 such that for all Q ≥ Q_0: Q^{−µ(T_l,T_{l−1})−δ} ≤ λ_i(Q) ≤ Q^{−µ(T_l,T_{l−1})+δ} for l = 1, …, r and d_{l−1} < i ≤ d_l (16.2), and T_{d_l}(Q) = T_l for l = 1, …, r (16.3).
hypotheses: Q_0 depends on δ and (L, c) and is not effective
proofSteps: For a subspace T defined over K of dimension k, restrict (L, c) to T and project to Q̄^n/T with the induced systems (L', c') and (L'', d) of (16.4)–(16.6) (EF Lemmas 16.2–16.3), comparing the successive infima of H_{L,c,Q} with those of the restriction and the quotient.

The upper bounds come from absolute-minkowski-for-twisted-heights applied to the blocks T_l/T_{l−1}; the lower bounds on each semistable block come from interval-result-semistable-case: outside finitely many bounded intervals the block has no point of height ≤ Q^{−µ−δ} (EF Lemma 16.4 and the induction on the filtration on pp. 73–78).
Lemmas 16.2–16.4 and the induction are not split into separate nodes here (gap).
acceptance: c = 0: the filtration is {0} ⊊ Q̄^n with µ = 0, and λ_i(Q) = 1 for all Q, consistent with (16.2).
Example with L = coordinates and c_∞ = (−1, 1) (filtration {0} ⊊ Q̄e_2 ⊊ Q̄²): λ_1(Q) = Q^{−1} and λ_2(Q) = Q, matching µ(T_1, T_0) = 1 and µ(T_2, T_1) = −1.

nodes.title: Height bound for the filtration subspaces (Evertse–Ferretti Proposition 17.5)
nodes.statement: Let (L, c) satisfy (2.4)–(2.7), let T_1, …, T_{r−1} be the subspaces of the filtration of Q̄^n with respect to (L, c), and H_2 := max{H_2(L_i^{(v)}) : v ∈ M_K, 1 ≤ i ≤ n}. Then H_2(T_i) ≤ H_2^{4^n} for i = 1, …, r − 1. In particular the exceptional subspace T(L, c) belongs to a finite, effectively determinable collection of subspaces depending only on L (Northcott for subspaces).
hypotheses: H_2 of linear forms = H_2 of coefficient vectors
proofSteps: Fix T = T_i, k = dim T, p = n − k, N = C(n, p) and the exterior-power system (L̂, ĉ) of (17.1)–(17.2); by EF (6.8), H_2(L̂_j^{(v)}) ≤ H_2^p.

By limit-of-successive-infima, for large Q, T_k(Q) = T and λ_k(Q)/λ_{k+1}(Q) ≤ Q^{−θ} (0 < θ < µ(T_{i+1}, T_i) − µ(T_{i+2}, T_{i+1})); EF Lemma 17.3 transfers this to λ̂_{N−1}(Q)/λ̂_N(Q) ≤ Q^{−θ/2}, so dim T̂_{N−1}(Q) = N − 1 and, again by limit-of-successive-infima for (L̂, ĉ), T̂_{N−1}(Q) = T̂ is a hyperplane in the filtration of (L̂, ĉ).

EF Lemma 17.4 bounds the height of a hyperplane in such a filtration by (max H_2(L̂))^{(N−1)²}; with EF Lemma 17.3(ii) (H_2(T_k(Q)) = H_2(T̂_{N−1}(Q))) this gives H_2(T) ≤ (H_2^p)^{(N−1)²} ≤ H_2^{4^n} since p(N − 1)² ≤ pC(n, p)² ≤ 4^n.
Lemmas 17.1–17.4 are not split into separate nodes here (gap).
acceptance: For L = coordinates (H_2 = 1) all filtration subspaces have height 1, i.e. are spanned by coordinate vectors (compare EF Lemma 15.3).
Effectivity: combined with finite_subspaceHeight_le this makes T(L, c) effectively computable, the effective half of DT.2's acceptance.

nodes.title: Absolute Parametric Subspace Theorem, quantitative (Evertse–Ferretti Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let n, L, c, δ, R satisfy (2.4)–(2.10). Then there are proper linear subspaces T_1, …, T_{t_0} of Q̄^n, all defined over K, with t_0 ≤ 10^6 2^{2n}n^{10}δ^{−3}log(3δ^{−1}R)log(δ^{−1}log 3R), such that for every real Q ≥ C_0 := max(H_L^{1/R}, n^{1/δ}) there is T_i ∈ {T_1, …, T_{t_0}} with {x ∈ Q̄^n : H_{L,c,Q}(x) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}} ⊂ T_i. Special case (EF Theorem 1.1): if Σ_i c_{iv} = 0, Σ_v max_i c_{iv} ≤ 1 and each {L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)}} ⊂ {X_1, …, X_n, X_1 + ⋯ + X_n} is linearly independent, then for 0 < δ ≤ 1 one can take Q ≥ n^{1/δ} and t_3 ≤ 10^6 2^{2n}n^{10}δ^{−3}(log(6nδ^{−1}))².
hypotheses: Standing notation (EF §§1–2): K ⊂ Q̄ a number field with places M_K and normalised absolute values ‖·‖_v (‖x‖_v = |σ_v(x)|^{[K_v:ℝ]/[K:ℚ]} at infinite v; the extension of |·|_p^{[K_v:ℚ_p]/[K:ℚ]} at v | p), which satisfy the product formula ∏_v ‖x‖_v = 1 on K^*; n ≥ 2; L = (L_i^{(v)} : v ∈ M_K, 1 ≤ i ≤ n) linear forms in K[X_1, …, X_n] with {L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)}} linearly independent for each v (2.5) and {L_1, …, L_r} := ∪_v {L_i^{(v)}} finite (2.6); c = (c_{iv}) reals with c_{iv} = 0 for all but finitely many v (2.7), Σ_i c_{iv} = 0 (2.8), Σ_v max_i c_{iv} ≤ 1 (2.9); 0 < δ ≤ 1, R ≥ r (2.10); Δ_L := ∏_v ‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v (2.11) and H_L := ∏_v max_{i_1<⋯<i_n} ‖det(L_{i_1}, …, L_{i_n})‖_v (2.12).
proofSteps: By interval-result, for Q ≥ C_0 with S_Q := {x : H_{L,c,Q}(x) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}} ⊄ T, Q lies in ∪_h ∪_{k=1}^s [Q_h^{(1+δ/2)^{k−1}}, Q_h^{(1+δ/2)^k}) with (1 + δ/2)^{s−1} < ω_0 ≤ (1 + δ/2)^s: at most 3δ^{−1}m_0(1 + log ω_0) intervals of the form [A, A^{1+δ/2}) with A ≥ C_0 ≥ n^{1/δ}.
By twisted-height-gap-principle, for each such interval the union of the S_Q lies in one proper subspace defined over K.
Adding the exceptional subspace T gives t_0 ≤ 1 + 3δ^{−1}m_0(1 + log ω_0), which is at most the stated bound.

nodes.title: Solutions of the system give small twisted heights (Evertse–Ferretti Lemma 5.1)
nodes.statement: Assume (3.1)–(3.6) (see absolute-subspace-theorem-for-systems), let K' be a finite Galois extension of K containing the coefficients of all L_i^{(v)}, and define (L, c, δ) over K' by (5.1)–(5.4): L_i^{(v)} := X_i and d_{iv} := 0 for v ∉ S, L_i^{(v')} := τ_{v'}^{−1}(L_i^{(v)}) and c_{i,v'} := d(v'|v)·(n/(n + ε))(d_{iv} − (1/n)Σ_j d_{jv}) for places v' | v of K', and δ := ε/(n + ε). If x ∈ Q̄^n solves (3.7) then with Q := H(x)^{1+ε/n}, H_{L,c,Q}(σ(x)) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ} for every σ ∈ Gal(Q̄/K). Moreover (L, c, δ) satisfies (2.4)–(2.10) over K' with R replaced by RD + n, and Δ_L = ∏_{v ∈ S}‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v, H_L ≤ n^{n/2}(H^*)^{DR}.
hypotheses: τ_{v'} ∈ Gal(K'/K) with ‖α‖_{v'} = ‖τ_{v'}(α)‖_v^{d(v'|v)} (the fixed extensions of ‖·‖_v to Q̄)
In the Lean prototype (forms and points over K, K' = K) the data (5.1)–(5.2) are the helper definitions systemForms and systemExponents
proofSteps: Pick a finite Galois E ⊇ K' containing σ(x); for w | v' | v put d_{iw} := d(w|v)d_{iv}, A_w := A_v^{d(w|v)} and choose τ_w with ‖α‖_w = ‖τ_w(α)‖_v^{d(w|v)}.
For v ∈ S, (3.7) gives ‖L_i^{(w)}(σ(x))‖_w/‖σ(x)‖_w ≤ A_wH(x)^{d_{iw}}; for v ∉ S the inequality is trivial (A_w = 1, forms X_i, d = 0). Σ_w Σ_i d_{iw} = −n − ε and ∏_w A_w = Δ_L^{1/n} (5.14).
With Q = H(x)^{1+ε/n}: ‖L_i^{(w)}(σx)‖_w Q^{−c_{iw}} ≤ A_w‖σx‖_w H(x)^{(1/n)Σ_j d_{jw}}; the product over w with H(σx) = H(x) gives Δ_L^{1/n}H(x)^{−ε/n} = Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}.
(2.4)–(2.10): immediate from (5.1)–(5.4), (3.2)–(3.5); H_L bound by Hadamard/ultrametric inequality (5.10).
acceptance: S = {∞}, n = 2, forms Y, X − αY over ℚ(α): the lemma turns a good rational approximation into a small point of a twisted height with two exponents.
The shift d_{iv} − (1/n)Σ_j d_{jv} makes Σ_i c_{iv} = 0 (EF (2.8)).

nodes.title: Absolute Subspace Theorem for systems of inequalities (Evertse–Ferretti Theorem 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let K ⊂ Q̄ be a number field, with a fixed extension of each ‖·‖_v (v ∈ M_K) to Q̄; let n ≥ 2, S ⊆ M_K finite, L_i^{(v)} (v ∈ S, 1 ≤ i ≤ n) linear forms with coefficients in Q̄ and d_{iv} reals such that {L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)}} is linearly independent for v ∈ S (3.1), H^*(L_i^{(v)}) ≤ H^* and [K(L_i^{(v)}) : K] ≤ D (3.2), #∪_{v∈S}{L_i^{(v)}} ≤ R (3.3), Σ_{v∈S}Σ_i d_{iv} = −n − ε with 0 < ε ≤ 1 (3.4), d_{iv} ≤ 0 (3.5), and A_v := ‖det(L_1^{(v)}, …, L_n^{(v)})‖_v^{1/n} (3.6). Then the solutions x ∈ Q̄^n of max_{σ ∈ Gal(Q̄/K)} ‖L_i^{(v)}(σ(x))‖_v/‖σ(x)‖_v ≤ A_vH(x)^{d_{iv}} (v ∈ S, i = 1, …, n) (3.7) with H(x) ≥ C_1 := max((H^*)^{1/3RD}, n^{n/ε}) lie in a union of at most 10^9 2^{2n}n^{14}ε^{−3}log(3ε^{−1}RD)log(ε^{−1}log 3RD) proper linear subspaces of Q̄^n, all defined over K. Here H^*(α_1X_1 + ⋯ + α_nX_n) := H(1, α_1, …, α_n) and H is the absolute height.
hypotheses: (3.1)–(3.6) as in the statement
Absolute setting: solutions in Q̄^n, max over Galois conjugates
proofSteps: Apply parametric-subspace-theorem over K' (Galois closure of the fields of the forms) to the (L, c, δ) of twisted-height-of-system-solutions, with 6(DR)² in place of R; then C'_0 ≤ C_1^{1+ε/n} (using H_L ≤ n^{n/2}(H^*)^{DR}) and the number of subspaces is at most the stated bound.
For a solution x with H(x) ≥ C_1 put Q := H(x)^{1+ε/n} ≥ C'_0; by twisted-height-of-system-solutions all conjugates σ(x) lie in {y : H_{L,c,Q}(y) ≤ Δ_L^{1/n}Q^{−δ}}, which is contained in one T_i.
Hence x ∈ T'_i := ∩_{σ} σ(T_i), a proper subspace defined over K.
acceptance: K = ℚ, S = {∞, p_1, …, p_s}, x ∈ ℤ^n primitive: (3.7) becomes |L_i^{(p)}(x)|_p/‖x‖_p ≤ A_p‖x‖^{d_{ip}}, the systems produced by product-inequality-reduces-to-systems; this is how p-adic-subspace-theorem follows.
Finiteness vs effectivity: the number of subspaces is explicit, the subspaces are not.

nodes.title: Interval refinement with an effective exceptional subspace (Evertse–Ferretti Theorem 3.3; Faltings–Wüstholz)
nodes.statement: Assume (3.1)–(3.6) and put m_1 := [10^8 2^{2n}n^{14}ε^{−2}log(3ε^{−1}RD)], ω_1 := 3nε^{−1}log 3RD. There are a proper linear subspace T of Q̄^n defined over K, which is effectively computable and belongs to a finite collection depending only on {L_i^{(v)} : v ∈ S, 1 ≤ i ≤ n}, and reals C_1 ≤ H_1 < ⋯ < H_{m_1} (C_1 as in absolute-subspace-theorem-for-systems) such that every solution x ∈ Q̄^n of (3.7) satisfies x ∈ T or H(x) ∈ [1, C_1) ∪ ∪_{h=1}^{m_1}[H_h, H_h^{ω_1}). In particular (3.7) has, up to scalar multiples, only finitely many solutions x ∈ K^n outside T (Faltings–Wüstholz, Theorem 9.1).
hypotheses: The H_h are ineffective; T is effective
proofSteps: Apply interval-result over K' to the (L, c, δ) of twisted-height-of-system-solutions (with 6(DR)² for R): m_0, ω_0 are bounded by m_1, ω_1 and C_0 ≤ C_1^{1+ε/n}.

EF Lemma 5.2 (merging intervals: [1, A_0) ∪ ∪[A_h, A_h^ω) ⊆ [1, B_0) ∪ ∪[B_h, B_h^{ω'}) for B_0 ≥ A_0, ω' ≥ ω, m' ≥ m) adjusts the constants; for x ∉ T' := ∩_σ σ(T(L, c)), Q = H(x)^{1+ε/n} lies in the union of intervals, whence the statement for H(x) with H_h := Q_h^{(1+ε/n)^{−1}}.

T' is effectively determinable from T(L, c), which is effectively computable and in a finite collection depending only on L by height-bound-for-filtration-subspaces and weight-and-exceptional-subspace.

Finitely many solutions outside T up to scalar multiples: the solutions are projective points of bounded height, and points of P^{n−1}(K) of bounded height are finite (Northcott: their normalised coordinates x_i/x_j have bounded height, and NumberField.finite_setOfPred_mulHeight₁_le applies).
acceptance: Vojta's refinement (vojta-effective-exceptional-subspaces) is the case K = ℚ, S = {∞} after reduction to systems.

nodes.title: The Q-vector space L of logarithms of algebraic numbers
nodes.statement: Define 𝓛 := {λ ∈ ℂ : e^λ is algebraic over ℚ} ⊆ ℂ. Since e^λ ≠ 0, 𝓛 is the set of all logarithms of nonzero algebraic numbers, where a logarithm of α ∈ ℂ^× is ANY λ ∈ ℂ with e^λ = α (no branch is fixed; the logarithms of α form the coset λ + 2πiℤ). 𝓛 is a ℚ-linear subspace of ℂ: e^{λ+μ} = e^λ e^μ, e^{-λ} = (e^λ)^{-1}, and for a/b ∈ ℚ (b ≥ 1) the number e^{aλ/b} is a root of X^b − (e^λ)^a. It is formalised as a Submodule ℚ ℂ, algebraicLogs. Conventions pinned for the whole stage: (i) algebraic means algebraic over ℚ (equivalently over ℤ, IsAlgebraic.restrictScalars); (ii) ℚ̄ denotes integralClosure ℚ ℂ, the algebraic numbers in ℂ, as in the Mathlib Lindemann-Weierstrass pull request; (iii) the principal logarithm is Mathlib's Complex.log, log z = log|z| + i·arg z with −π < arg z ≤ π, and Complex.cpow is x^y = exp(log x · y) for x ≠ 0; every theorem of this stage is stated for arbitrary logarithms (elements of 𝓛) and the principal-branch versions are corollaries. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.algebraicLogs.
proofSteps: Carrier {λ | IsAlgebraic ℚ (exp λ)}; zero_mem: exp 0 = 1 is algebraic (isAlgebraic_one).
add_mem: exp (λ + μ) = exp λ · exp μ (Complex.exp_add) and products of algebraic numbers are algebraic (IsAlgebraic.mul).

smul_mem for q = a/b ∈ ℚ: (exp(qλ))^b = exp(aλ) = (exp λ)^a when a ≥ 0 and = ((exp λ)^{-1})^{|a|} otherwise (Complex.exp_nat_mul, Complex.exp_int_mul, IsAlgebraic.inv), which is algebraic; IsAlgebraic.of_pow with b > 0 gives that exp(qλ) is algebraic.
acceptance: 2πi·k ∈ 𝓛 for every k ∈ ℤ, while Complex.log never takes the value 2πi: 𝓛 is strictly larger than the set of principal logarithms of algebraic numbers.
log 2 ∈ 𝓛 although log 2 is transcendental: membership in 𝓛 is not algebraicity of λ.

nodes.title: A finite set of algebraic numbers lies in a finite Galois subfield of ℂ
nodes.statement: Let S ⊆ ℂ be a finite set of algebraic numbers. There is an intermediate field L of ℂ/ℚ with S ⊆ L, [L : ℚ] < ∞ and L/ℚ Galois. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.exists_isGalois_superset.
hypotheses: S finite
every s ∈ S algebraic over ℚ
proofSteps: Let f be the product of the pairwise distinct minimal polynomials minpoly ℚ s, s ∈ S; distinct monic irreducible polynomials over ℚ are coprime and separable (characteristic 0), so f is separable.

Put L := ℚ(rootSet f ℂ). Since ℂ is algebraically closed, f splits in ℂ and L is a splitting field of f over ℚ (IntermediateField.adjoin_rootSet_isSplittingField); it is finite-dimensional, being generated by finitely many algebraic elements.
A splitting field of a separable polynomial is Galois (IsGalois.of_separable_splitting_field); each s ∈ S is a root of its minimal polynomial, hence of f, hence lies in L.
acceptance: S = {√2, i}: L = ℚ(√2, i) of degree 4 works, while ℚ(√2 + i) (also of degree 4) is the same field — the lemma asserts existence only.

nodes.title: A nonzero algebraic integer of a Galois subfield of ℂ has a Galois conjugate of absolute value at least 1
nodes.statement: Let L be an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ with [L : ℚ] < ∞ and L/ℚ Galois, and let x ∈ L be integral over ℤ with x ≠ 0. Then there is τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ) with |τ(x)| ≥ 1 (absolute value in ℂ). (Evertse, Lemma 3.6, for an element of a Galois subfield.) Proposed declaration: Transcendence.exists_one_le_norm_algEquiv.
hypotheses: L ⊆ ℂ, FiniteDimensional ℚ L, IsGalois ℚ L
x ∈ L, IsIntegral ℤ x, x ≠ 0
proofSteps: By NumberField.exists_conjugate_one_le_norm (applied to x as a nonzero element of 𝓞 L) there is a ring homomorphism σ : L → ℂ with ‖σ x‖ ≥ 1.
Since L/ℚ is normal and σ, the inclusion ι : L → ℂ are ℚ-algebra maps into ℂ, AlgHom.restrictNormal' gives τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ) with ι ∘ τ = σ (AlgHom.restrictNormal_commutes); hence |τ(x)| = ‖σ x‖ ≥ 1.

nodes.title: Size inequality for nonzero algebraic numbers (the fundamental inequality of transcendence)
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d, σ : K → ℂ a field embedding, x ∈ K with x ≠ 0, and m ≥ 1 an integer with m·x integral over ℤ. Then 1 ≤ m^d · |σ(x)| · house(x)^{d−1}, where house(x) = max_τ |τ(x)| over all embeddings τ : K → ℂ (NumberField.house). Equivalently |σ(x)| ≥ m^{−d} house(x)^{−(d−1)}. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.one_le_pow_mul_norm_mul_house_pow.
hypotheses: K number field, d = [K : ℚ]
m ∈ ℕ, m ≥ 1, IsIntegral ℤ (m·x)
proofSteps: y := m·x is a nonzero algebraic integer of K, so its norm N_{K/ℚ}(y) is a rational number that is integral over ℤ (Algebra.isIntegral_norm), hence an integer (ℤ is integrally closed), and it is nonzero (Algebra.norm_ne_zero_iff); so |N(y)| ≥ 1.
NumberField.norm_norm_le_norm_mul_house_pow gives |N(y)| ≤ |σ(y)| · house(y)^{d−1}.
|σ(y)| = m|σ(x)| and house(y) = m·house(x) (NumberField.house_nat_mul); hence 1 ≤ m·|σ(x)|·m^{d−1}house(x)^{d−1} = m^d|σ(x)|house(x)^{d−1}.
acceptance: d = 1, K = ℚ: the inequality says |x| ≥ 1/m for a nonzero rational with denominator dividing m.
x = (1 − √5)/2, m = 1, σ the identity: |x| ≈ 0.618 ≥ house(x)^{-1} ≈ 0.618 (equality).

nodes.title: Hermite's theorem: e is transcendental
nodes.statement: e = exp(1) is transcendental: Transcendental ℤ (Complex.exp 1). (Evertse, Theorem 4.1.) Proposed declaration: transcendental_e.
proofSteps: Suppose e is algebraic. Take Q ∈ ℤ[X], Q ≠ 0, Q(e) = 0; dividing by the largest power of X dividing Q (Polynomial.exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd at 0, and e ≠ 0) we may assume Q(0) ≠ 0. Write Q = q_0 + q_1X + ... + q_nX^n with q_0 ≠ 0 (Evertse (4.1)).

Apply LindemannWeierstrass.exp_polynomial_approx to f := (X − 1)(X − 2)⋯(X − n) ∈ ℤ[X], f(0) = (−1)^n n! ≠ 0: there is c such that for every prime p > n! there are n_p ∈ ℤ with p ∤ n_p and g_p ∈ ℤ[X] with |n_p e^a − p g_p(a)| ≤ c^p/(p−1)! for a = 1, …, n. This packages Evertse's Lemma 4.2 (the integral identity, Mathlib's integral_exp_mul_eval), Lemma 4.4 (the estimate), Lemma 4.5 (the derivative values of the polynomial (4.3), which is X^{p−1}f^p/(p−1)!) and the estimate of Lemma 4.7.
N_p := n_p q_0 + p Σ_{a=1}^{n} q_a g_p(a) is an integer, and p ∤ N_p for every prime p > max(n!, |q_0|) (Evertse Lemma 4.6).

Multiplying Q(e) = 0 by n_p gives N_p = −Σ_{a=1}^{n} q_a (n_p e^a − p g_p(a)), hence |N_p| ≤ (Σ|q_a|) c^p/(p−1)!, which is < 1 for all large p (FloorSemiring.tendsto_pow_div_factorial_atTop). Choosing such a prime (Nat.exists_infinite_primes) gives N_p = 0, contradicting p ∤ N_p (Evertse Lemma 4.7 and the concluding paragraph).
acceptance: Transcendental ℤ (Real.exp 1) follows: Complex.ofReal is an injective ℤ-algebra map with ofReal (Real.exp 1) = Complex.exp 1.

The theorem is also the case a = 1 of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/hermite-lindemann-transcendence-of-exp; this node gives the self-contained proof of §4.1, which uses no Galois theory.

nodes.title: Galois conjugation of formal exponential sums
nodes.statement: Let L be an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ and τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ) = (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L). galConj τ : L[L] ≃+* L[L] is the ring automorphism Σ_γ δ_γ [γ] ↦ Σ_γ τ(δ_γ) [τ(γ)], acting on exponents and coefficients simultaneously; it is the composite of AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainRingEquiv for the additive automorphism τ of L and AddMonoidAlgebra.mapRingEquiv for the ring automorphism τ. An element x is Galois-fixed (galConj τ x = x for all τ) exactly when every τ permutes the pairs (γ, δ_γ) with δ_γ ≠ 0 — Evertse's hypothesis in Theorem 4.11. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.galConj.
hypotheses: L : IntermediateField ℚ ℂ
τ : L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L
proofSteps: galConj τ := (mapDomainRingEquiv L τ.toAddEquiv).trans (mapRingEquiv L τ.toRingEquiv); both factors are ring isomorphisms because τ is additive (for the domain) and a ring automorphism (for the coefficients).
acceptance: galConj τ (single γ δ) = single (τ γ) (τ δ).
For L = ℚ(√2) and τ(√2) = −√2 the element [√2] + [−√2] is Galois-fixed, while [√2] is not.

nodes.title: M_k as a sum of Hermite integrals (Evertse Lemma 4.12(i))
nodes.statement: Let L be an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ and x ∈ L[L] with expEval L x = 0. Then for all l, p ∈ ℕ and γ ∈ L: (auxValue x l p γ : ℂ) = Σ_{γ' ∈ supp x} δ_{γ'} · F_{f}(γ'), where f = auxPoly (supp x) l p γ mapped to ℂ[X] and F is Hermite's integral. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.coe_auxValue_eq_sum_hermiteIntegral.
hypotheses: expEval L x = 0
proofSteps: expEval L x = Σ_{γ'} δ_{γ'} e^{γ'} = 0 (expEval_apply); apply DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/sum-hermite-integral-of-exp-relation to the family (γ', δ_{γ'}) and the polynomial f.
sumIDeriv commutes with mapping coefficients L → ℂ (Polynomial.sumIDeriv_map) and evaluation commutes with the inclusion (Polynomial.eval_map), so the right-hand side is the image of auxValue in ℂ.

nodes.title: Derivatives of f_k at the points γ_j (Evertse Lemma 4.13)
nodes.statement: Let L be a number field inside ℂ, S ⊆ L finite with t = |S|, γ ∈ S, l ≥ 1 an integer with l·γ' integral over ℤ for all γ' ∈ S, and p a prime. Let f = auxPoly S l p γ and A_γ := l^t ∏_{γ' ∈ S, γ' ≠ γ} (γ − γ'). Then (i) f^{(p−1)}(γ) = A_γ^p, and A_γ is integral; (ii) f^{(j)}(γ') = 0 for γ' ∈ S, 0 ≤ j ≤ p − 1 and (γ', j) ≠ (γ, p − 1); (iii) for γ' ∈ S and j ≥ p, f^{(j)}(γ')/p is integral over ℤ. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.eval_iterate_derivative_auxPoly.
hypotheses: l ≥ 1 and l·γ' integral for γ' ∈ S
p prime
γ ∈ S
proofSteps: (i), (ii): f = (X − γ)^{p−1}·h with h(γ) = l^{tp}∏(γ − γ')^p/(p−1)!, and f = (X − γ')^p·h' for γ' ≠ γ; Polynomial.aeval_iterate_derivative_self and aeval_iterate_derivative_of_lt give the values. A_γ = l·∏_{γ'≠γ}(lγ − lγ') is integral.

(iii): g := (p−1)!·f(X/l) = l·(X − lγ)^{p−1}∏_{γ'≠γ}(X − lγ')^p has integral coefficients. By Polynomial.exists_iterate_derivative_eq_factorial_smul (Evertse (4.8)), g^{(j)} = j!·h_j with h_j integral; hence f^{(j)}(γ') = l^j g^{(j)}(lγ')/(p−1)! = l^j (j!/(p−1)!) h_j(lγ'), and p divides j!/(p−1)! for j ≥ p.

sources.match: Part (iii); parts (i), (ii) are (4.13), (4.14).

nodes.title: M_γ is a nonzero algebraic integer for large p (Evertse Lemma 4.14)
nodes.statement: Let L be a number field inside ℂ of degree d, x ∈ L[L] whose coefficients δ_{γ'} are algebraic integers, l ≥ 1 an integer with l·γ' integral for γ' ∈ S = supp x, and γ ∈ S. Let A_γ be as in Lemma 4.13. Then for every prime p > |N_{L/ℚ}(δ_γ) · N_{L/ℚ}(A_γ)|, auxValue x l p γ is integral over ℤ and nonzero. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.isIntegral_auxValue and LindemannWeierstrass.auxValue_ne_zero.
hypotheses: coefficients of x integral
l·γ' integral for γ' ∈ supp x
p prime, p > |N(δ_γ) N(A_γ)|
proofSteps: By Lemma 4.13, auxValue x l p γ = −δ_γ A_γ^p − p·ξ with ξ integral (the terms j ≥ p contribute multiples of p, the terms j < p vanish except (γ, p−1)); so it is integral.
δ_γ ≠ 0 and A_γ ≠ 0 (the points of S are distinct), so N(δ_γ), N(A_γ) are nonzero integers (Algebra.norm_ne_zero_iff, Algebra.isIntegral_norm).

If auxValue = 0 then δ_γ A_γ^p/p is integral, so its norm N(δ_γ)N(A_γ)^p/p^d is an integer (N(p) = p^d, Algebra.norm_algebraMap); but p ∤ N(δ_γ)N(A_γ) because p exceeds its absolute value, a contradiction.
acceptance: L = ℚ, x = [0] (δ = 1, S = {0}), l = 1: auxValue = −1 ≠ 0 for every p.

nodes.title: The numbers M_k tend to 0 (Evertse Lemma 4.15, Exercise 4.3)
nodes.statement: Let L be an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ, x ∈ L[L] with expEval L x = 0 and support S, and l ≥ 1. There are real C, c > 0 such that for every p ≥ 1 and every γ ∈ S: |auxValue x l p γ| ≤ C·c^p/(p−1)!. In particular |auxValue x l p γ| < 1 for all γ ∈ S and all sufficiently large p. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.norm_auxValue_le.
hypotheses: expEval L x = 0
proofSteps: By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-auxiliary-value-eq-hermite-sum, auxValue x l p γ = Σ_{γ'∈S} δ_{γ'} F_f(γ') with f = auxPoly S l p γ.
Let R := max(1, max_{γ'∈S}|γ'|) and t := |S|. For |u| ≤ R each factor |u − γ''| ≤ 2R, so |f(u)| ≤ l^{tp}(2R)^{tp−1}/(p−1)! ≤ c^p/(p−1)! with c := (2Rl)^t.
By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/norm-hermite-integral-le, |F_f(γ')| ≤ R e^R c^p/(p−1)!; sum over γ' with C := (Σ|δ_{γ'}|) R e^R.
c^p/(p−1)! → 0 (FloorSemiring.tendsto_pow_div_factorial_atTop).

nodes.title: Weak Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem (Evertse Theorem 4.11)
nodes.statement: Let L be an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ, finite and Galois over ℚ, and let x ∈ L[L] be nonzero and fixed by every Galois conjugation galConj τ, τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ). Then expEval L x ≠ 0. Equivalently: if γ_1, …, γ_t ∈ L are distinct, δ_1, …, δ_t ∈ L are nonzero and every τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ) permutes the pairs (γ_k, δ_k), then δ_1 e^{γ_1} + ⋯ + δ_t e^{γ_t} ≠ 0. Proposed declaration: LindemannWeierstrass.expEval_ne_zero_of_forall_galConj_eq.
hypotheses: FiniteDimensional ℚ L, IsGalois ℚ L
∀ τ, galConj τ x = x
proofSteps: Suppose expEval L x = 0. By Algebra.IsAlgebraic.exists_integral_multiples there is m ∈ ℤ \ {0} with m·δ_γ integral for all γ; m·x is still nonzero, Galois-fixed, with expEval = 0. So assume the coefficients integral.
Choose an integer l ≥ 1 with l·γ integral for all γ in the (nonempty) support S (same lemma), and fix γ_1 ∈ S.

By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-auxiliary-value-small choose a prime p exceeding |N(δ_{γ_1})N(A_{γ_1})| with |auxValue x l p γ| < 1 for all γ ∈ S (Nat.exists_infinite_primes).

M := auxValue x l p γ_1 is a nonzero algebraic integer (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-auxiliary-value-integral-nonzero), and for each τ, τ(M) = auxValue x l p (τγ_1) with τγ_1 ∈ S (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-auxiliary-value-galois-permutation), so |τ(M)| < 1 for all τ.
This contradicts DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/nonzero-integer-has-large-conjugate.
acceptance: The Galois-fixed hypothesis cannot be dropped in the proof method (though the conclusion holds in general by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-weierstrass-in-bakers-form).

nodes.title: The Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem in Baker's form
nodes.statement: Let ℚ̄ = integralClosure ℚ ℂ. For every injective family u : ι → ℚ̄, the family (e^{u_i})_{i∈ι} is linearly independent over ℚ̄: linearIndependent_exp u u_inj : LinearIndependent ℚ̄ (fun i ↦ exp (u i)). Equivalently (Evertse Theorem 4.8): if α_1, …, α_n ∈ ℚ̄ are pairwise distinct and β_1, …, β_n ∈ ℚ̄ are nonzero, then β_1e^{α_1} + ⋯ + β_ne^{α_n} ≠ 0. Proposed declaration: linearIndependent_exp.
hypotheses: u injective (the α_i pairwise distinct)
coefficients in ℚ̄ (for the equivalent form: all β_i ≠ 0)
proofSteps: By linearIndependent_iff' it suffices to show: a finite relation Σ_{i∈s} v_i e^{u_i} = 0 with v_i ∈ ℚ̄ forces v = 0. Suppose some v_i ≠ 0.

By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/galois-subfield-containing-finite-set there is a finite Galois L ⊆ ℂ containing all u_i, v_i (i ∈ s). Put x := Σ_{i∈s} v_i [u_i] ∈ L[L]: x ≠ 0 since the u_i are distinct, and expEval L x = 0.

Put P := ∏_{τ ∈ Gal(L/ℚ)} galConj τ x. Each factor is nonzero (galConj τ is injective) and L[L] has no zero divisors: (L, +) is a ℚ-vector space, so it has TwoUniqueSums (instTwoUniqueSumsOfModuleRat), hence UniqueSums, and AddMonoidAlgebra.instNoZeroDivisorsOfUniqueSums applies. So P ≠ 0. This replaces Evertse's argument with the lexicographic order on ℂ, which is exactly a unique-sum argument.
P is Galois-fixed (galConj_prod_galConj) and expEval L P = ∏_τ expEval L (galConj τ x) = 0 because the factor τ = id is expEval L x = 0.
This contradicts DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-weierstrass-weak-form.

The two anonymous Mathlib instances this proof uses are found by typeclass inference and are not cited as prerequisites: NoZeroDivisors R[A] for A with UniqueSums (the additive form of the instance at Mathlib/Algebra/MonoidAlgebra/NoZeroDivisors.lean:91) and TwoUniqueSums G for every ℚ-vector space G (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/UniqueProds/VectorSpace.lean:22).
acceptance: α = (0, 1), β = (1, −e): the coefficient −e is not algebraic, and indeed 1·e^1 − e·e^0 = 0 — the coefficients must be algebraic.
With α_1 = α_2 the sum (β_1 + β_2)e^{α_1} vanishes when β_2 = −β_1: injectivity is essential.

Evertse states that Theorem 4.8 is equivalent to the classical Lindemann-Weierstrass theorem (algebraic independence form), which is DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/algebraic-independence-of-exponentials.

nodes.title: Lindemann-Weierstrass, algebraic independence form (Evertse Corollary 4.10)
nodes.statement: If u : ι → ℚ̄ is a family of algebraic numbers that is linearly independent over ℚ (stated, as in the Mathlib pull request, as LinearIndependent ℕ u, which for a ℚ-vector space is equivalent), then (e^{u_i})_i is algebraically independent over ℚ̄: algebraicIndependent_exp. Proposed declaration: algebraicIndependent_exp.
hypotheses: u linearly independent over ℕ (equivalently over ℤ or ℚ)
proofSteps: Let P ∈ ℚ̄[X_i] be nonzero, P = Σ_{k∈I} β_k X^k with β_k ≠ 0. Then P(e^{u}) = Σ_k β_k e^{Σ_i k_i u_i} (Complex.exp_sum, Complex.exp_nat_mul).

By linear independence the exponents Σ k_i u_i, k ∈ I, are pairwise distinct; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/lindemann-weierstrass-in-bakers-form gives P(e^u) ≠ 0 (algebraicIndependent_iff).
acceptance: For u = (1, √2): e and e^{√2} are algebraically independent.
u = (1, 2) is not linearly independent and indeed (e^1)^2 − e^2 = 0.

nodes.title: Schanuel's conjecture (as a proposition)
nodes.statement: SchanuelConjecture : Prop is the statement: for every n ∈ ℕ and every x : Fin n → ℂ that is linearly independent over ℚ, the transcendence degree over ℚ of the field ℚ(x_1, …, x_n, e^{x_1}, …, e^{x_n}) is at least n; formally (n : Cardinal) ≤ Algebra.trdeg ℚ ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range x ∪ Set.range (exp ∘ x))). It is a statement to be formalised, never assumed as an axiom: results depending on it take SchanuelConjecture as an explicit hypothesis. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.SchanuelConjecture.
proofSteps: Definition of the proposition by the displayed formula.
acceptance: For n = 1 the statement holds unconditionally (Evertse Example 1): for x ≠ 0 either x is transcendental or e^x is (DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/hermite-lindemann-transcendence-of-exp).
For algebraic x it holds unconditionally (Evertse Example 2, from DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/algebraic-independence-of-exponentials).

sources.excerpt: Schanuel’s Conjecture. (1960’s) Let x1, . . . , xn be any (not necessarily algebraic) complex numbers that are linearly independent over Q. Then trdeg(x1, . . . , xn, ex1, . . . , exn) ⩾ n.
sources.match: Exactly the conjecture; trdeg is over Q (Evertse's definition at the start of Chapter 4).

nodes.title: Schanuel's conjecture implies that e and π are algebraically independent
nodes.statement: Assume SchanuelConjecture. Then e and π are algebraically independent over ℚ: AlgebraicIndependent ℚ ![Real.exp 1, Real.pi] (as complex numbers). Proposed declaration: Transcendence.SchanuelConjecture.algebraicIndependent_exp_one_pi.
hypotheses: SchanuelConjecture
proofSteps: Apply the conjecture to x = (1, πi), which is ℚ-linearly independent since πi ∉ ℚ: trdeg ℚ ℚ(1, πi, e, e^{πi}) ≥ 2.

ℚ(1, πi, e, −1) ⊆ ℚ(i, π, e), which is algebraic over ℚ(π, e) (i is algebraic); hence trdeg ℚ ℚ(e, π) ≥ 2: a transcendence basis of the larger field can be chosen inside {e, π} (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.trdeg_le_cardinalMk bounds the transcendence degree of a field algebraic over the algebra generated by a set by the cardinality of the set).
A family of 2 generators of a field of transcendence degree ≥ 2 is a transcendence basis (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isTranscendenceBasis_of_le_trdeg_of_finite), hence algebraically independent.
acceptance: The hypothesis πi ∉ ℚ is where 'never forget to verify this condition' (Evertse) applies.

sources.excerpt: So by Schanuel’s conjecture, trdeg(e, π) = trdeg(e, πi) = trdeg(1, πi, e, eπi) = 2. Here we used that 1 and πi are linearly independent over Q (never forget to verify this condition!).
sources.match: The conditional proof.

λ_i ∈ 𝓛
λ ℚ-linearly independent

n generators with trdeg ≥ n are algebraically independent (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isTranscendenceBasis_of_le_trdeg_of_finite).

nodes.title: Rolle's theorem counts zeros: f' has at least one zero fewer than f
nodes.statement: Let f : ℝ → ℝ be differentiable and S a finite nonempty set of zeros of f. Then there is a finite set T of zeros of f' with |T| = |S| − 1; its elements separate consecutive elements of S. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.exists_finset_card_deriv_zeros.
hypotheses: f differentiable on ℝ
S finite, S ≠ ∅, f = 0 on S
proofSteps: List S increasingly s_1 < ⋯ < s_N. For each k < N, Rolle's theorem (exists_deriv_eq_zero) on [s_k, s_{k+1}] gives t_k ∈ (s_k, s_{k+1}) with f'(t_k) = 0.
The open intervals are pairwise disjoint, so t_1, …, t_{N−1} are distinct; T := {t_k}.

nodes.title: Real zeros of a real exponential polynomial (Evertse Lemma 4.23, Exercise 4.5)
nodes.statement: Let r ≥ 1, let γ_1, …, γ_r be distinct real numbers and p_1, …, p_r ∈ ℝ[X] nonzero polynomials, and put M := Σ_{k=1}^{r} (1 + deg p_k) and E(x) := Σ_k p_k(x) e^{γ_k x}. Then E has at most M − 1 real zeros: every finite set of real zeros of E has at most M − 1 elements. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.card_zeros_expPoly_le.
hypotheses: γ_k ∈ ℝ pairwise distinct
p_k ∈ ℝ[X], p_k ≠ 0
proofSteps: Induction on r. For r = 1, E(x) = 0 iff p_1(x) = 0, and p_1 has at most deg p_1 = M − 1 roots (Polynomial.card_roots').

For r ≥ 2, G(x) := e^{−γ_r x}E(x) = p_r(x) + Σ_{k<r} p_k(x)e^{(γ_k−γ_r)x} has the same zeros (Real.exp_ne_zero). Differentiating D := deg p_r + 1 times kills p_r, and (q(x)e^{λx})' = (q' + λq)(x)e^{λx} with λ = γ_k − γ_r ≠ 0 keeps each p_k nonzero of the same degree; so G^{(D)} is an exponential polynomial with r − 1 terms and M' = M − D.
By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/rolle-zero-count applied D times, #zeros(E) ≤ #zeros(G^{(D)}) + D ≤ (M − D − 1) + D = M − 1 (induction hypothesis).
acceptance: E(x) = e^x − e^{2x}: M = 2, one zero (x = 0).
E(x) = x e^{0·x} − 1·e^{0·x} is excluded: the exponents must be distinct (combine to (x − 1), M = 2, one zero).

sources.excerpt: Lemma 4.23. Assume that the γk and the coeﬃcients of the pk are all reals. Put M := Pr k=1(1 + deg pk). Then E(z) has at most M −1 zeros in R.

nodes.title: Dividing an entire function by its zeros (Evertse Lemma 4.24, with multiplicities)
nodes.statement: Let f : ℂ → ℂ be entire, a_1, …, a_s ∈ ℂ distinct and k_1, …, k_s ∈ ℕ such that f^{(j)}(a_i) = 0 for all i and all j < k_i. Then there is an entire g with f(z) = g(z) ∏_i (z − a_i)^{k_i} for all z ∈ ℂ. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.exists_differentiable_eq_mul_prod_pow.
hypotheses: f entire (Differentiable ℂ f)
a_i distinct
iteratedDeriv j f a_i = 0 for j < k_i
proofSteps: Induction on Σ k_i. Pick i with k_i ≥ 1; then f(a_i) = 0, and g_1 := dslope f a_i is entire (Complex.differentiableOn_dslope) with f(z) = (z − a_i)g_1(z) (sub_smul_dslope).

Orders of vanishing add under products (analyticOrderAt_mul); z − a_i has order 1 at a_i and 0 elsewhere, so g_1 vanishes to order ≥ k_i − 1 at a_i and ≥ k_j at a_j (j ≠ i); translate between orders and derivatives with natCast_le_analyticOrderAt_iff_iteratedDeriv_eq_zero and apply the induction hypothesis.
acceptance: f = sin(πz) with zeros at 0, ±1: g entire with sin(πz) = g(z) z(z − 1)(z + 1).

sources.excerpt: Lemma 4.24. Let f be an entire function and a ∈ C a zero of f. Then there is an entire function g such that f(z) = g(z) · (z −a) for z ∈ C.

nodes.title: An entire function with many zeros in a disc is small there (Evertse Lemma 4.26, with multiplicities)
nodes.statement: Let f be entire, a_1, …, a_s distinct with |a_i| ≤ R, and k_i ∈ ℕ with f^{(j)}(a_i) = 0 for j < k_i; put K := Σ k_i. Let 0 < R and T ≥ 3R, and M ≥ 0 with |f(w)| ≤ M for all |w| = T. Then |f(z)| ≤ M·(3R/T)^K for all |z| ≤ R. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.norm_le_of_zeros.
hypotheses: f entire
|a_i| ≤ R, a_i distinct
|f| ≤ M on |w| = T
proofSteps: By DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/entire-function-divided-by-zeros, f = g·∏(z − a_i)^{k_i} with g entire.

For |w| = T, |w − a_i| ≥ T − R ≥ 2T/3, so |g(w)| ≤ M(3/(2T))^K; by the maximum modulus principle (Complex.norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le on the disc of radius T; Evertse Lemma 4.25) the same bound holds for |z| ≤ T.
For |z| ≤ R, |∏(z − a_i)^{k_i}| ≤ (2R)^K; multiply.
acceptance: f(z) = z^K, a_1 = 0, k_1 = K: |z|^K ≤ T^K (3R/T)^K holds for |z| ≤ R.

nodes.title: Schneider's auxiliary function via Siegel's lemma (Evertse Lemma 4.22)
nodes.statement: Setting S: K ⊆ ℂ is a number field (an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ of finite degree d), l ∈ ℂ and β ∈ K with α := e^l ∈ K and γ := e^{βl} ∈ K. Constants c_i depend only on (K, l, β), never on the parameters L, D_1, D_2, a, b. There is c_1 > 0 such that for all integers L ≥ 3 and D_1, D_2 ≥ 1 with D_1D_2 ≥ 2dL² there are a_{ij} ∈ 𝓞_K (0 ≤ i < D_1, 0 ≤ j < D_2), not all zero, with house(a_{ij}) ≤ exp(c_1(D_1 log L + D_2L)), such that F(z) := Σ_{i,j} a_{ij} z^i e^{jlz} vanishes at z = a + bβ for all a, b ∈ {1, …, L}. For integers a, b ≥ 0, F(a + bβ) is the image of y_{ab} := Σ_{i,j} a_{ij}(a + bβ)^i α^{aj}γ^{bj} ∈ K. Proposed declaration: GelfondSchneider.exists_schneider_auxiliary.
hypotheses: Setting S: K ⊆ ℂ is a number field (an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ of finite degree d), l ∈ ℂ and β ∈ K with α := e^l ∈ K and γ := e^{βl} ∈ K. Constants c_i depend only on (K, l, β), never on the parameters L, D_1, D_2, a, b.
L ≥ 3, D_1D_2 ≥ 2dL²
proofSteps: e^{jl(a+bβ)} = α^{aj}γ^{bj} (Complex.exp_nat_mul, Complex.exp_add), so the vanishing conditions are the L² linear equations Σ a_{ij}(a + bβ)^iα^{aj}γ^{bj} = 0 in the D_1D_2 unknowns a_{ij}.

Let m ≥ 1 be an integer with mα, mβ, mγ integral (Algebra.IsAlgebraic.exists_integral_multiples); multiplying by m^{D_1+2LD_2} makes all coefficients integral, with house ≤ m^{D_1+2LD_2}L^{D_1}H^{D_1+2LD_2}, H := 1 + house α + house β + house γ (NumberField.house_mul_le, house_add_le, house_pow_le), which is ≤ exp(c_2(D_1 log L + D_2L)) since log L ≥ 1.

Apply NumberField.house.exists_ne_zero_int_vec_house_le with p = L² equations and q = D_1D_2 unknowns (L² < D_1D_2); since p/(q − p) ≤ 1 the bound c(c q A)^{p/(q−p)} is ≤ exp(c_1(D_1 log L + D_2L)). (If the coefficient matrix is zero, take a_{00} = 1.)

Evertse uses the version of Siegel's lemma with rational-integer solutions (his Theorem 3.20); Mathlib's lemma gives algebraic-integer solutions, which serve equally: all later estimates use house(a_{ij}).

nodes.statement: Setting S: K ⊆ ℂ is a number field (an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ of finite degree d), l ∈ ℂ and β ∈ K with α := e^l ∈ K and γ := e^{βl} ∈ K. hypotheses: Setting S: K ⊆ ℂ is a number field (an intermediate field of ℂ/ℚ of finite degree d), l ∈ ℂ and β ∈ K with α := e^l ∈ K and γ := e^{βl} ∈ K. Constants c_i depend only on (K, l, β), never on the parameters L, D_1, D_2, a, b.
β ∉ ℚ

Parameters: M ≥ 1 an integer, L := 2dM², D_1 := (2d)²M³, D_2 := 2dM (so D_1 = √(2d)L^{3/2}, D_2 = √(2d)L^{1/2}, D_1D_2 = 2dL²), c := 1 + ⌊√(2d)⌋, and F, a_{ij}, y_{ab} as in Lemma 4.22 (node DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/schneider-auxiliary-function) for these parameters.
proofSteps: Put R := (1 + |β|)cL and T := 3eR; every a + bβ with 1 ≤ a, b ≤ cL lies in |z| ≤ R.

For |z| ≤ T: |z^i e^{jlz}| ≤ T^{D_1} e^{D_2T|l|} and |a_{ij}| ≤ house(a_{ij}) (NumberField.norm_embedding_le_house), so sup_{|z|=T}|F| ≤ D_1D_2 exp(c_1(D_1 log L + D_2L)) T^{D_1}e^{D_2T|l|} ≤ exp(c_4L^{3/2} log L). (This corrects the printed factor (1 + |α|)^{Tj}, false for 0 < α < 1; see sourceIssues.)

The L² numbers u + vβ (1 ≤ u, v ≤ L) are pairwise distinct zeros of F (β ∉ ℚ) of modulus ≤ R; DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/schwarz-lemma-many-zeros with 3R/T = e^{−1} gives |F(z)| ≤ exp(c_4L^{3/2} log L)·e^{−L²} for |z| ≤ R.

nodes.statement: Let ρ_1, …, ρ_N ∈ ℂ be pairwise distinct and c ∈ ℂ^N, c ≠ 0. Then the entire function E(z) := Σ_i c_i e^{ρ_i z} is not identically zero; consequently its order of vanishing analyticOrderAt E z_0 is finite at every z_0 ∈ ℂ. Proposed declaration: Transcendence.sum_mul_exp_ne_zero.

nodes.title: Division of an entire function of n variables by z_k − ζ, with bounds
nodes.statement: Let f : ℂ^n → ℂ be entire, k ∈ {1, …, n} and ζ ∈ ℂ. Put f_0(z) := f(z with z_k replaced by ζ) and g(z) := ∫_0^1 (∂_k f)(z with z_k replaced by ζ + t(z_k − ζ)) dt. Then g is entire and f = f_0 + (z_k − ζ)·g. If 0 ≤ |ζ| ≤ r < R then |f_0|_R ≤ |f|_R and |g|_R ≤ 2|f|_R/(R − r). If f is a polynomial of degree ≤ e in some variable z_j, so are f_0 and g, and for j = k, g has degree ≤ e − 1 in z_k. Norms: for z ∈ ℂ^n, |z| = max_i |z_i| (Mathlib's sup norm on Fin n → ℂ) and ‖z‖ = Σ_i |z_i|; for σ ∈ ℕ^n, |σ| = max σ_i, ‖σ‖ = Σ σ_i, σ! = ∏ σ_i!; for f entire on ℂ^n, |f|_R := sup_{|z| ≤ R} |f(z)| (in Lean: a bound hypothesis ∀ z ∈ closedBall 0 R, ‖f z‖ ≤ M). Proposed declaration: Baker.exists_div_sub_single.
hypotheses: f entire on ℂ^n
|ζ| ≤ r < R for the bounds
proofSteps: The fundamental theorem of calculus along t ↦ ζ + t(z_k − ζ) gives f(z) − f_0(z) = (z_k − ζ)g(z) (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt).

g is complex-differentiable by differentiation under the integral sign (hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le), since ∂_kf is entire. This replaces the appeal to the Osgood-Hartogs fact in the source.

For fixed other coordinates and |z_k| = R: |g| = |f(z) − f_0(z)|/|z_k − ζ| ≤ 2|f|_R/(R − r); the maximum modulus principle in the variable z_k (Complex.norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le) extends this to |z_k| ≤ R. |f_0|_R ≤ |f|_R is immediate.
Degree statements: expand f in z_j; the operations are coefficientwise.

nodes.title: Division by a polynomial in one variable, with bounds (Waldschmidt Lemma 4.8, case m = n)
nodes.statement: Let P ∈ ℂ[X] be monic of degree p with all roots in the disc |ζ| ≤ r, let 0 < 5r ≤ R, k ∈ {1, …, n}, and f entire on ℂ^n. There are unique entire f_0, f_k with f = f_0 + f_k·P(z_k) and f_0 a polynomial in z_k of degree < p. Moreover |f_0|_R ≤ 3^p|f|_R and |f_k|_R ≤ (3/R)^p|f|_R; if f is a polynomial of degree ≤ e in z_j (j ≠ k) so are f_0 and f_k. Finally, if (∂_k)^κ f vanishes on {z_k = ζ} for every root ζ of P and every κ < m_P(ζ) (the multiplicity), then f_0 = 0, i.e. f = f_k·P(z_k). Norms: for z ∈ ℂ^n, |z| = max_i |z_i| (Mathlib's sup norm on Fin n → ℂ) and ‖z‖ = Σ_i |z_i|; for σ ∈ ℕ^n, |σ| = max σ_i, ‖σ‖ = Σ σ_i, σ! = ∏ σ_i!; for f entire on ℂ^n, |f|_R := sup_{|z| ≤ R} |f(z)| (in Lean: a bound hypothesis ∀ z ∈ closedBall 0 R, ‖f z‖ ≤ M). Proposed declaration: Baker.exists_div_polynomial.
hypotheses: P monic of degree p, roots in |ζ| ≤ r
proofSteps: Existence and bounds by induction on p (Step 2.4): write P = (X − ζ)Q; by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/several-variable-division-by-linear-factor, f = f(ζ) + (z_k − ζ)g with |g|_R ≤ 2|f|_R/(R − r); by induction g = g_0 + Q(z_k)f_k; put f_0 := f(ζ) + (z_k − ζ)g_0. The constants satisfy A_p = 1 + 2A_{p−1}(R + r)/(R − r) ≤ 3^p and (2/(R − r))^p ≤ (3/R)^p because R ≥ 5r.
Uniqueness (Steps 2.2-2.3): if f_0 + f_kP(z_k) = 0 then f_0, a polynomial in z_k of degree < p, is divisible by P(z_k), hence 0.

Vanishing criterion: under the vanishing hypothesis, for fixed other coordinates f_0 is a polynomial in z_k of degree < p with roots of total multiplicity ≥ p (Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_le_iff, Polynomial.card_roots'), so f_0 = 0.
acceptance: P = X^p, r = 0: f_0 is the Taylor polynomial of degree < p in z_k, and f_k the remainder divided by z_k^p.

Proposed declaration: Baker.exists_div_cartesian.

proofSteps: Induction on the number of variables handled, m = n, n − 1, …, 1 (Step 3): divide by P_m(z_m) with DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/several-variable-division-by-one-variable-polynomial, then apply the induction hypothesis to both quotients; the degree conditions are preserved (Step 3.2) and the constants C_m = 3^{p(n−m)}(1 + 2p)^{n−m−1} satisfy C_m ≤ 9^{(n−m+1)p} (Step 3.6).

Vanishing (Steps 3.3, 3.5): f_0 satisfies the vanishing conditions; fixing all variables but z_m, f_0 is a polynomial in z_m of degree < p_m with roots of total multiplicity ≥ p_m, so its z_m-coefficients vanish on the remaining Cartesian product; conclude by induction and the uniqueness of the one-variable case.

nodes.statement: Let E_1, …, E_n ⊆ ℂ be finite sets with S_1 elements each, E := E_1 × ⋯ × E_n, r > 0 with r ≥ max_i max_{ζ∈E_i} |ζ|, and R ≥ 18^n r. nodes.title: Interpolation by the truncated Taylor expansion (Waldschmidt Lemma 4.13, variant)
nodes.statement: Let 0 < r < R, T a positive integer and F entire on ℂ^n. Then |F|_r ≤ (1 + T)(r/R)^T|F|_R + Σ_{‖τ‖<T} |D^τF(0)|·r^{‖τ‖}/τ!. (The source has the factor 1 + √T, obtained with Parseval's formula; the factor 1 + T follows from Cauchy's inequalities and suffices for every use.) Proposed declaration: Baker.norm_le_truncatedTaylor.
hypotheses: 0 < r < R
proofSteps: G := F − Σ_{‖τ‖<T} D^τF(0) z^τ/τ!. Take z_0 with |z_0| = r and |F(z_0)| = |F|_r and put f(w) := F(z_0w), g(w) := G(z_0w); g vanishes to order ≥ T at w = 0.

One-point Schwarz lemma: by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.3/entire-function-divided-by-zeros, g = w^T h with h entire, and the maximum modulus principle gives |g(1)| ≤ (r/R)^T |g|_{R/r}.
P := f − g = Σ_{t<T} a_t w^t with |a_t| ≤ |f|_{R/r}(R/r)^{−t} (Cauchy); hence |P|_{R/r} ≤ T|f|_{R/r} and |g|_{R/r} ≤ (1 + T)|F|_R.
acceptance: For a polynomial F of total degree < T the first term is not needed: G = 0.

nodes.title: An exponential polynomial with distinct frequencies vanishes identically only if all coefficients vanish
nodes.statement: Let λ_1, …, λ_r ∈ ℂ be pairwise distinct and p_1, …, p_r ∈ ℂ[X]. If Σ_k p_k(s)e^{λ_k s} = 0 for all s ∈ ℂ, then p_1 = ⋯ = p_r = 0. Proposed declaration: Baker.eq_zero_of_sum_polynomial_mul_exp.
hypotheses: λ_k pairwise distinct
proofSteps: Induction on Σ_{p_k≠0}(1 + deg p_k), discarding zero p_k. Multiply by e^{−λ_r s} and differentiate deg p_r + 1 times: p_r disappears, and (q(s)e^{μs})' = (q' + μq)(s)e^{μs} with μ = λ_k − λ_r ≠ 0 keeps every other nonzero coefficient nonzero of the same degree; the induction hypothesis forces all of them to vanish, a contradiction unless r = 1, where p_1(s)e^{λ_1 s} ≡ 0 gives p_1 = 0 (Complex.exp_ne_zero, a polynomial with infinitely many roots is 0).

nodes.title: The functions z^τ e^{(tx)·z} are linearly independent
nodes.statement: Let 0 ≤ d_0 ≤ n and x_1, …, x_{d_1} ∈ ℂ^n be linearly independent over ℚ. Then the functions z ↦ z_1^{τ_1}⋯z_{d_0}^{τ_{d_0}} e^{(t_1x_1+⋯+t_{d_1}x_{d_1})·z} on ℂ^n, for (τ, t) ∈ ℕ^{d_0} × ℕ^{d_1}, are linearly independent over ℂ. Proposed declaration: Baker.linearIndependent_monomial_exp.
hypotheses: x_1, …, x_{d_1} linearly independent over ℚ
d_0 ≤ n
proofSteps: Distinct t ∈ ℕ^{d_1} give distinct vectors w_t := Σ t_ix_i (ℚ-linear independence).

Suppose Σ_{τ,t} c_{τt} z^τ e^{w_t·z} ≡ 0 with some c ≠ 0 and group it as Σ_t P_t(z)e^{w_t·z} with polynomials P_t, some P_{t_0} ≠ 0.
